modules.name: Node canvas, typed ports and accessible editing
modules.design_question: Which browser node canvas and typed-port scheme lets designers wire Layer 0 and module outputs accessibly, with type, unit, cycle and cardinality errors rejected on every edit path and a non-drag alternative for every drag?
inputs: Module manifests with port declarations (P15-M03)
User edits: add, connect (click), move, group, collapse, paste, undo/redo
Layer 0 typed ports and staged documents with schema_version (owner P14-M01; true north from P14-M03 Layer0Georef)
outputs: Graph document JSON: nodes {id, module@version, params, enabled}, edges {fromPort, toPort}, revision id
Port-type registry: type id (Layer 0 class + schema_version) -> JSON Schema $id, dimension, unit
Connection-rejected events with the expected type, unit and reason
Outline table view model of nodes, ports and edges with connect and disconnect actions

parameters.name: connection_rule (exact versioned type id | declared subtype | via converter node)
parameters.relationship: Stricter rule -> fewer invalid wires reach execution but more converter nodes. Ports carry type version plus physical dimension, so metre-to-foot or length-to-area wires need an explicit converter. React Flow lets the app veto UI connections (isValidConnection).

parameters.name: type_id_versioning (P14-M01 class + schema_version)
parameters.relationship: Port type id = Layer 0 class plus schema_version (major.minor while 0.y.z, where MINOR is breaking). A breaking change makes a new id, so old graphs fail loudly instead of mis-wiring. Owner: P14-M01; deprecation window is a maintainer decision.

parameters.name: layer0_port_set_freeze (team target 1 Nov 2026)
parameters.relationship: Every typed port depends on the Layer 0 schema. Freezing the port set before the core build stops ids changing under it; later changes ship as migrations with new type ids. The person who owns the freeze is not yet recorded (see flags).

parameters.name: site_frame (units, CRS, true_north_deg, north_type)
parameters.relationship: Sun, shadow and wind modules read true_north_deg and north_type from Layer0Georef (P14-M03), released only after the user confirms. P15 stores no angle of its own. A wrong angle rotates every shadow by that angle.

parameters.name: cycle_policy (reject in the graph model on every edit path)
parameters.relationship: A cycle -> no topological order exists, so the graph cannot execute. The check runs in the graph-model reducer, so paste, import, undo/redo and programmatic setEdges cannot create one either.

parameters.name: port_cardinality (item | list | tree)
parameters.relationship: Tree ports (path -> branch -> item) let one module evaluate many floors or towers in one run, as Grasshopper data trees do; the matching rule is set in P15-M02. Adds a concept users must learn.

parameters.name: canvas_library (xyflow | Rete | Baklava | litegraph)
parameters.relationship: A maintained library with a large user base lowers forced-migration risk; an archived or stale one raises it. Observed push dates and weekly downloads are in the metrics.

parameters.name: collapsed_groups, required labels, onlyRenderVisibleElements
parameters.relationship: Collapsing node trees (hidden) or rendering only viewport elements lowers rendered node count and re-render cost. Required group labels are secondary notation that helps a teammate read the graph; named clusters with typed ports are v1.

parameters.name: drag_inventory (every pointer-drag and its single-pointer alternative)
parameters.relationship: Connect -> click source then target; move -> numeric x/y fields; pan -> buttons calling setViewport; edge reconnect -> edgesReconnectable=false (delete, then connect); marquee -> shift-click or outline checkboxes; minimap -> view-only; resize -> numeric fields.

parameters.name: handle_hit_area (>= 24 CSS px, never overlapping)
parameters.relationship: WCAG 2.5.8 ignores page zoom and excludes overlapping areas. Counter-scale handle areas only up to the point they would intersect; below a zoom threshold hide handles and connect from the outline view (Equivalent exception).

parameters.name: category_stripe_and_status_encoding
parameters.relationship: Thirteen category codes: print the code on every stripe and cap hue families at 8 plus lightness variants (team assumption), since many hues are hard to tell apart, especially with colour-vision deficiency. Chips pair icon and text and follow current_status.

parameters.name: decided_by_strip (code | ai | person)
parameters.relationship: Node cards show a three-segment strip (letters C, A, P plus colour) built from manifest decided_by, so a reader sees who decided each threshold. The three roles map to PROV software agent and person.

metrics.name: Discrete-interaction latency (Event Timing, durationThreshold 16 ms, p98)
metrics.method: Playwright script on the reference VTC graph in Chromium: click-to-connect, key presses, parameter input, run button. PerformanceObserver type 'event' with durationThreshold 16; p98 over ALL scripted interactions, unreported ones counted as 16 ms.
metrics.basis: Event Timing never exposes continuous events and hides entries under the threshold (default 104 ms), so the r1 drag method measured nothing. web.dev INP bands are field p75; borrowing them for a lab p98 is a team assumption.

metrics.name: Drag, pan and zoom frame time (p95)
metrics.method: Scripted node drag, pan and zoom on the reference graph; record requestAnimationFrame deltas and report p95. Long Animation Frames (over 50 ms) are a secondary signal where the browser supports them.
metrics.basis: Continuous events are not exposed by Event Timing, so frames are measured. 16.7 ms is the 60 Hz budget (arithmetic); the 33.3 ms line and p95 are team presets. LoAF support outside Chromium is unverified.

metrics.name: Pointer target size of handles and buttons (SC 2.5.8)
metrics.good: >= 24 x 24 CSS px at minZoom, zoom 1 and maxZoom, or the spacing or Equivalent exception (handles hidden, outline view offered)
metrics.bad: < 24 x 24 CSS px without an exception
metrics.method: Automated DOM measurement of every interactive element at minZoom, 1 and maxZoom, plus manual review of exceptions. Overlapping areas are not counted toward target size.
metrics.basis: WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8, Level AA (verified): independent of page zoom, overlap excluded, Equivalent and Essential (dense visualisation) exceptions. Applying it to canvas zoom is our reading.

metrics.name: Handle hit areas never intersect
metrics.good: 0 intersecting handle pairs at every zoom in range
metrics.method: DOM bounding-box intersection test on the dense reference graph at minZoom, 1 and maxZoom; counter-scaling is capped at the intersection limit.
metrics.basis: Counter-scaling is our design; the overlap exclusion comes from the 2.5.8 page. Below the zoom threshold handles hide and the outline view is the Equivalent route.

metrics.name: Single-pointer non-drag alternative for every drag action
metrics.good: Every enabled drag prop has a listed non-drag alternative and passes a click-only test
metrics.bad: Any drag-only action (connect, move, resize, pan, reconnect, marquee, minimap)
metrics.method: Playwright enumerates React Flow props (nodesDraggable, panOnDrag, selectionOnDrag, edgesReconnectable, MiniMap pannable, NodeResizer) and fails if one is enabled without an alternative; a click-only script then runs each alternative.
metrics.basis: r1 listed connect, move, resize only. React Flow enables panOnDrag and edgesReconnectable by default. SC 2.5.7 examples: map direction buttons, click-click connecting lines, area selection by two clicks. Applying it to node editors is our reading.

metrics.name: Keyboard operability of graph editing (SC 2.1.1)
metrics.good: Add, connect, disconnect, move, toggle and delete all work by keyboard, via canvas focus or the outline view
metrics.bad: Any editing function needs a mouse; if the outline view slips, report 'not met in core' on the canvas
metrics.method: Playwright keyboard-only script plus a screen-reader pass (NVDA or VoiceOver) on the outline view.
metrics.basis: SC 2.1.1 requires all functionality by keyboard (verified). React Flow documents Tab, Enter or Space and arrow-key moves, not keyboard connect, so the outline view supplies it.

metrics.name: Outline view design and focus order
metrics.good: Plain table with Connect and Disconnect buttons, numeric x/y and a defined focus order ships in core
metrics.method: Checklist review plus Playwright focus-order assertion.
metrics.basis: Team design rule that delivers SC 2.1.1 and the Equivalent exception for small targets; it is not itself a WCAG requirement.

metrics.name: Non-text contrast of ports, wires and status chips (SC 1.4.11)
metrics.good: >= 3:1 against adjacent colours
metrics.method: Automated contrast check of theme tokens in light and dark mode.
metrics.basis: WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.11 Non-text Contrast, Level AA.

metrics.name: Category and status encoding without colour
metrics.good: Every stripe prints its category code; <= 8 hue families; chips pair icon with text; ports differ by shape or label
metrics.bad: Colour is the only cue, or > 8 hue families
metrics.method: Review against a colour-vision-deficiency simulation; automated check that every stripe and chip carries text.
metrics.basis: SC 1.4.1 forbids colour as the only cue (verified); the 8-family cap and port-shape rule are team design rules.

metrics.name: Invalid connections accepted by the model (any edit path)
metrics.method: Property test over UI wiring, paste, template import, undo/redo and programmatic setEdges: random port pairs are accepted only when type, unit, cycle and cardinality rules allow.
metrics.basis: Course requirement that outputs are typed inputs of the next node; zero tolerance is our policy. isValidConnection guards only UI wiring, so the rule lives in the reducer.

metrics.name: Canvas library maintenance health
metrics.good: Not archived and pushed within 90 days
metrics.bad: Archived, or no push for more than 12 months
metrics.method: Read GitHub pushed_at and archived flag; npm weekly downloads. Observed 21 Oct 2026: xyflow pushed 2026-10-20 (8.35 M/week); Rete 2026-10-18 (47 k); Baklava 2026-09-16 (1.7 k); litegraph.js 2024-08-01; Comfy-Org fork archived (2026-01-14).
metrics.basis: Threshold days are an editable team preset; the observed values are verified.

metrics.name: Interactive node/edge capacity at 60 fps on a mid-range laptop
metrics.good: unverified: to be benchmarked
metrics.method: Benchmark synthetic graphs of increasing size with and without onlyRenderVisibleElements; React Flow's performance guide gives no node-count figures.
metrics.basis: No published sourced figure found.

visualization: Node cards: category stripe with printed code (SITE, CLIM...), title, input ports left, output ports right, a current_status chip (icon and text) with a history icon for corrected claims, and a three-segment decided_by strip (C, A, P).
Ports shaped by type (circle item, square list, diamond tree) with unit label and version chip; colour is never the only cue; collapsible legend.
A rejected connection shows a red dashed ghost wire and a tooltip such as 'expects layer0.FloorPlate@schema_version [m2], got table [ft2]'.

Outline table of every node, port and edge with Connect, Disconnect and x/y fields and ARIA names such as 'Daylight node, input layer0.Tower, connected from Massing'; pan and zoom buttons beside the canvas.
Below the zoom threshold handles hide with a pointer to the outline; read-only minimap; labelled group frames.
modules.method: Build on @xyflow/react. Custom nodes are generated from manifests (P15-M03); each Handle carries a versioned port-type id, dimension and unit from the P14-M01 Layer 0 schema. The graph JSON is the single source of truth. Type, unit, cycle (getOutgoers) and cardinality rules run in the graph-model reducer, so UI wiring, paste, import, undo/redo and setEdges share one check; P15-M02 re-checks at load. Drag props follow the drag inventory (edgesReconnectable off, selectionOnDrag off, MiniMap pannable off, NodeResizer off in core) and a Playwright test fails on any enabled drag prop lacking an alternative. Click-to-connect plus a plain-table outline view (Connect, Disconnect, numeric x/y) give click, keyboard and screen-reader paths; buttons pan through setViewport. Hit areas are counter-scaled up to the intersection limit; below the zoom threshold handles hide. Keep React Flow attribution visible unless a Pro plan is bought.

modules.name: DAG execution, run modes, matching and provenance
modules.design_question: How does the tool run a wired graph reproducibly, keep the edit loop responsive, let users run all or step into one node, and record inputs, thresholds, sources, environment and who decided each value?
inputs: Graph JSON (P15-M01)
Validated manifests (P15-M03)
Layer 0 payload with snapshot hash and schema_version
Per-node enabled flag and user threshold overrides
External datasets as hashed input nodes (content hash, retrieval date)
outputs: RunRecord JSON (RFC 8785): run_id, graph revision and hash, Layer 0 snapshot hash and schema_version, environment block {platform version, browser and engine, runtime versions, seed}

Per node: module@version, parameter values each with decided_by {code|ai|person, actor, date}, input hashes, outputs, metrics with threshold basis, source ids and current_status, mode, items_repeated stamp, duration, error, bypass stamp
Typed node results consumed by downstream nodes
Stale, blocked, progress and cancel state map for the canvas

parameters.name: execution_mode (auto | run-all | step-into) and default
parameters.relationship: Default auto for T0 and formula nodes (debounced) and run-all for heavy nodes (last run over 1 s), with a stale hatch and the mode stamped in the RunRecord. Auto keeps the edit loop fresh; run-all caps cost. Trust effects are unsourced.

parameters.name: auto_debounce (preset 250 ms, team assumption)
parameters.relationship: Longer debounce -> fewer wasted re-runs but later feedback. Nielsen: 0.1 s feels instant and 1 s keeps flow of thought, so the whole T0 loop (debounce plus run) should stay under 1 s. The 250 ms value is tuned in the pilot.

parameters.name: cache_key = hash(module@version, parameters, upstream hashes, external-data hashes, seed, matching rule)
parameters.relationship: Same key -> reuse the cached output; changed key -> recompute that node and its descendants. Rete's dataflow engine caches outputs and needs an explicit reset when inputs change.

parameters.name: topological schedule (Kahn)
parameters.relationship: Ordering nodes so each runs after its inputs costs O(V+E); edges left over after the queue empties reveal a cycle, so a cyclic graph is refused.

parameters.name: matching_rule (longest-list default | strict for metric nodes; graft/flatten)
parameters.relationship: Longest-list is Grasshopper's documented default: shorter streams keep their last value until all run dry. That repetition can create a pass/fail nobody asked for, so repeats are stamped; strict mode errors on length mismatch. The rule enters the cache key.

parameters.name: run_feedback_and_cancel (progress, cancel, timeout)
parameters.relationship: Over 1 s show a working state; over 10 s show a percent-done bar and a clearly marked Cancel. Longer budget -> fewer false kills but a longer stall. Default cancel is Worker.terminate; a Pyodide SharedArrayBuffer interrupt needs isolation headers and is optional.

parameters.name: disabled_node_mode (block default | bypass via declared passthrough ports)
parameters.relationship: Block marks every descendant blocked, so no verdict is computed on missing data. Bypass is allowed only through a manifest-declared passthrough port pair, and downstream results are stamped 'computed with X bypassed'. One enum for the tool (P15-M07 reuses it).

parameters.name: threshold_override (editable team assumption)
parameters.relationship: Editing a threshold changes the cache key of every dependent node and records decided_by = person with actor and date, so the run shows the value actually used and who set it.

parameters.name: decided_by_in_runrecord (code | ai | person)
parameters.relationship: Every parameter, threshold and metric value carries who decided it: code for computed values, person for overrides, ai for AI-drafted manifest fields until a named person confirms them. This is the course rule separating code, AI and people.

parameters.name: numeric_tolerance (per-metric; exact hash only on the same engine and version)
parameters.relationship: ECMAScript lets engines approximate functions such as sin and exp, so last digits can differ across browsers. Compare across engines within a declared per-metric tolerance; compare exact canonical-JSON hashes only on the same engine and version.

parameters.name: external_data_inputs (hashed dataset nodes)
parameters.relationship: A dataset enters as an input node whose content hash and retrieval date join the cache key; a changed dataset gives a new key and a recompute instead of a stale result that still looks complete.

metrics.name: Determinism (same engine and version)
metrics.good: 100% identical canonical-JSON hashes on two consecutive runs with the same inputs, versions and seed; across engines every numeric output within its declared tolerance
metrics.bad: Any same-engine hash difference, or a cross-engine difference beyond tolerance
metrics.method: Serialise with RFC 8785 (sorted keys, ECMAScript number formatting); run twice in CI on Chromium and Firefox; compare hashes per engine and values across engines within tolerance.
metrics.basis: Course requirement that results show their work; thresholds are our policy. Fixed-precision rounding is avoided because boundary values flip.

metrics.name: Provenance completeness
metrics.good: 100% of result values carry module@version, parameters, input hash, threshold basis, source id and current_status, decided_by with actor and date, Layer 0 snapshot hash and the run's environment block
metrics.method: Schema check of every RunRecord entry.
metrics.basis: Course requirement: every result cites its source, shows its work and separates what code, AI and people decide.

metrics.name: Scheduling cost
metrics.good: O(V+E)
metrics.method: Kahn or DFS topological sort.
metrics.basis: Standard algorithm complexity.

metrics.name: Discrete-interaction latency during a run (Event Timing p98)
metrics.good: <= 200 ms, and p95 frame time <= 33.3 ms
metrics.method: Heavy modules run in workers. During scripted run-all, record Event Timing (durationThreshold 16) for discrete interactions and rAF frame deltas; p98 over all interactions, unreported counted as 16 ms.
metrics.basis: INP bands are field p75; continuous events are not exposed, so the r1 label and method were corrected twice. Bands are team presets.

metrics.name: Incremental re-run time after one parameter change
metrics.good: <= 1 s for T0 and formula nodes; <= 10 s acceptable for others
metrics.bad: > 10 s without a percent-done bar and a Cancel control
metrics.method: Wall-clock of a warm-cache re-run on the reference VTC graph, reported per node class.
metrics.basis: Nielsen's 0.1, 1 and 10 s limits (1993, updated 2014), a sourced HCI guideline applied by our reading. The r1 presets of 5 s and 30 s had no source.

metrics.name: Progress and cancel coverage for runs over 10 s
metrics.good: 100% of runs expected to exceed 10 s show a percent-done bar and a Cancel control within 1 s of starting
metrics.bad: Any run over 10 s lacking either
metrics.method: Slow fixture node plus UI test; Cancel must terminate the worker.
metrics.basis: Nielsen: percent-done indicator and a signposted interrupt beyond 10 s; the 1 s display lag is a team preset.

metrics.name: Stale-result marking
metrics.good: 100% of results older than their inputs show the stale hatch before the next user action
metrics.bad: Any stale result shown as current
metrics.method: Edit an upstream parameter in a test graph and assert every descendant hatches.
metrics.basis: Policy so stale numbers are not read as current; comprehension is tested in P15-M09.

metrics.name: Repeated-item stamp coverage
metrics.good: 100% of matches that repeat items are stamped in the RunRecord and on the wire; strict mode rejects length mismatch
metrics.method: Fixtures with unequal list lengths in longest-list and strict modes.
metrics.basis: McNeel documents that Longest List runs until all streams run dry; silent repetition can produce an unrequested verdict. Earlier text called the default design logic and cited the wrong source.

metrics.name: Bypass/block stamp coverage
metrics.good: 100% of results downstream of a disabled node carry 'blocked' or 'computed with X bypassed' in the RunRecord and on the chip
metrics.method: Reachability test from every toggled node over the reference graph.
metrics.basis: Design policy so a pass/fail verdict never silently changes meaning.

visualization: Node status chips (idle, stale hatch, running, ok, warn, error, blocked, bypassed) with a pulse along wires during a run, a percent-done bar and a Cancel button on long runs.
Wires show a 'repeated items' stamp when longest-list repeats values.
Core view: RunRecord table with decided_by strip per value and a 'download provenance' button; bottom timeline (Gantt) of per-node durations.
v1 step-into side panel in three columns: Inputs (hash, preview) | Method, parameters, thresholds with source links | Outputs with pass/fail badges and environment block.
Run-diff table between two RunRecords (v1).
modules.method: Load the graph, validate it against manifests (P15-M03) and port rules (P15-M01), Kahn-sort and refuse cycles. For each node compute the cache key; on a hit reuse the output, otherwise call the runtime (first-party code or the T0 evaluator now; P15-M04 sandbox later), validate with Ajv and append a RunRecord entry. Auto mode runs T0 and formula nodes after a debounce; heavy nodes run on request; stale results are hatched. Matching defaults to longest-list with repeats stamped; metric nodes can run strict. Over 1 s show a working state, over 10 s a percent-done bar and Cancel (Worker.terminate). Each value carries decided_by. RunRecords are RFC 8785 JSON with the Layer 0 snapshot hash and schema_version. A failed node blocks descendants; disabled nodes follow the toggle enum. Results are immutable; any edit makes a new run.

modules.name: Module manifest, shared status vocabulary, decided_by and T0 modules
modules.design_question: What manifest makes every module self-describing, source-cited, safely renderable and machine-checkable, with one status vocabulary and a record of whether code, AI or a person decided each value?
inputs: manifest.json per module
Module bundle and test fixtures
Taxonomy enumerations (13 category codes, 5 phases, 4 jury tags, 4 statuses, 3 decided_by roles)
SPDX licence list
Source extracts and visualization payload samples
outputs: Validated manifest object
Port-type registry entries (versioned)
Lint report (errors and warnings)
Module-card data for palette, registry and review (P15-M05, P15-M06)
Visualization-payload validation result

parameters.name: id and name rules
parameters.relationship: A unique lowercase id keeps forks distinct and saved graphs resolvable. VS Code requires lowercase names, Obsidian a unique id, Yak restricted characters, crates.io case-insensitive collision checks.

parameters.name: version (SemVer 2.0.0; 0.y.z handling)
parameters.relationship: The number encodes change impact: a backward-incompatible schema change raises MAJOR. In 0.y.z anything may change, so a MINOR bump inside 0.x counts as breaking (^0.2.3 stays below 0.3.0), or listing requires 1.0.0.

parameters.name: category, phase, jury_tags (enumerations)
parameters.relationship: Category decides palette placement and colour; jury tags let a dashboard aggregate which criteria a graph evidences. VS Code similarly limits categories to a fixed list.

parameters.name: inputs / outputs as JSON Schema 2020-12, direction-aware diff
parameters.relationship: Typed ports derive from schemas. Narrowing an input, or widening an output, breaks consumers because they receive values they never handled; adding an optional output field is compatible. Design logic, unsourced.

parameters.name: parameters[] with relationship text, unit, source_ids, decided_by
parameters.relationship: A required causal relationship stops a module hiding assumptions; empty relationship or missing decided_by -> lint error.

parameters.name: current_status and history[] (one shared enum)
parameters.relationship: current_status {verified | team_assumption | unverified | false} sets chip colour and source rules; history[] {was_false_in, corrected_in, evidence} keeps corrections visible without colouring a valid value as wrong. The same enum serves M01 badges, M03 and M06 flags.

parameters.name: decided_by {code | ai | person}, actor, date
parameters.relationship: Every parameter, threshold and metric names who decided it. AI-drafted fields stay below 'verified' until a named person confirms; lint rejects a missing decided_by. Roles map to PROV software agent and person, with ai acting on behalf of a person.

parameters.name: visualization contract (declarative payload types)
parameters.relationship: A module returns typed payloads (chart spec, grid, mesh, table, text) that first-party code renders; no HTML, SVG strings, URLs or expressions. Otherwise module markup is an XSS risk and image requests, governed by img-src, can carry data out.

parameters.name: output_caps (max bytes, list length, vertices)
parameters.relationship: Unbounded outputs can exhaust memory or freeze rendering; the manifest declares caps and the host enforces them at the message boundary. Numeric defaults await benchmarking.

parameters.name: source_extract_policy (max words, clause numbers)
parameters.relationship: Standards such as NBC/VBBL, ASHRAE and CSA are copyrighted: store clause numbers and derived numeric thresholds, never tables or clauses. Extracts are capped (preset 25 words). Team policy, not legal advice.

parameters.name: t0_declarative_module (formula plus thresholds as data)
parameters.relationship: Most evaluation modules are a formula plus thresholds, so a JSON module run by a first-party evaluator needs no code execution. A restricted grammar limits risk; mathjs' own docs admit unknown parser vulnerabilities and advise a killable worker.

parameters.name: licence (SPDX expression)
parameters.relationship: The declared licence decides who may fork and redistribute; a missing licence means no reuse rights.

parameters.name: permissions[] and runtime tier (T0-T3)
parameters.relationship: Each declared permission widens what the sandbox grants; a new permission in an update forces re-approval, as Chrome does. T0 modules need none.

parameters.name: engines (platform version range)
parameters.relationship: Declares compatible platform versions so incompatible modules are not loaded, as VS Code's engines.vscode field does.

metrics.name: Manifest schema validity
metrics.good: 0 validation errors
metrics.method: Ajv validation at editor save, registry CI and graph load.
metrics.basis: CI gate policy; validator mechanism is standard JSON Schema.

metrics.name: Threshold classification coverage
metrics.good: 100% of thresholds have current_status verified (with at least one opened source), team_assumption, unverified or false
metrics.bad: Any unclassified threshold, or verified without a source
metrics.method: Lint rule over metrics[].
metrics.basis: Course requirement: unsourced thresholds appear as editable team assumptions.

metrics.name: decided_by coverage and AI confirmation
metrics.good: 100% of parameters, thresholds and metrics carry decided_by with actor and date; no ai-drafted value is 'verified' without a named person's confirmation
metrics.bad: Any missing decided_by, or an unconfirmed ai value marked verified
metrics.method: Lint rule over the manifest plus RunRecord schema check.
metrics.basis: Course rule to separate what code, AI and people decide; the field design is ours, with PROV agent types as model.

metrics.name: Single status vocabulary
metrics.good: One enum {verified, team_assumption, unverified, false} in M01 chips, M03 manifests and M06 flags; a corrected claim shows its current_status chip plus a history icon
metrics.bad: Any other value, or history colouring a valid value as false
metrics.method: Unit test over schemas and UI tokens; comprehension is tested in P15-M09.
metrics.basis: r1 mixed current state with history (false_assumption_corrected as a status) and three vocabularies; policy fix.

metrics.name: SemVer compliance
metrics.good: No breaking input/output schema diff without a MAJOR bump (a MINOR bump inside 0.y.z counts as the breaking bump)
metrics.bad: Breaking diff shipped as PATCH, or as MINOR at >= 1.0.0
metrics.method: Compare two manifest versions' schemas (removed or narrowed inputs, widened or retyped outputs) and compare with the bump.
metrics.basis: SemVer 2.0.0: backward-incompatible change -> MAJOR; 0.y.z is initial development; released versions are immutable. The 0.x caret convention is a team choice.

metrics.name: Direction-aware diff fixtures
metrics.good: Input narrowing and output widening are both flagged breaking; an added optional output field is flagged compatible
metrics.method: Vitest fixtures with paired manifest versions.
metrics.basis: Design logic; no JSON Schema standard defines port variance.

metrics.name: Licence field validity
metrics.good: Valid SPDX expression; code licence is OSI-approved
metrics.method: Parse with spdx-expression-parse; check against the SPDX list with its OSI-approved flag.
metrics.basis: SPDX License List identifiers and OSI flag.

metrics.name: Source link health
metrics.good: All source URLs resolve at CI time
metrics.bad: Any 404 or 403 without an archived copy
metrics.method: HEAD requests in CI; opened flag recorded per source.
metrics.basis: Team policy; several sources in this packet returned 403, so a fallback is needed.

metrics.name: Test presence
metrics.good: >= 1 passing fixture per metric
metrics.method: Run fixtures in Vitest; compare outputs with expected values.
metrics.basis: JOSS requires an automated test suite or documented manual tests; no numeric coverage threshold is set because none was sourced.

metrics.name: Visualization payload validity
metrics.good: 100% of payloads validate against the declarative schema and size caps, with 0 URL, markup or expression strings
metrics.bad: Any payload with a URL, markup or expression, or above caps
metrics.method: Ajv validation plus a string scan; Vega specs run only through the CSP-safe interpreter.
metrics.basis: Design policy to keep module output data-only; img-src governs image requests; the Vega interpreter avoids Function and eval.

metrics.name: Source extract length
metrics.good: <= 25 words per extract and no copied tables or clauses
metrics.bad: Longer extract, or a copied table or clause
metrics.method: CI length check plus a reviewer checklist item.
metrics.basis: Editable preset; copyright caution for standards text, not legal advice.

visualization: Manifest editor form with live inline validation (red/green).
Module card in the palette: category stripe with code, version, SPDX badge, tier badge, stacked bar of verified / team assumption / unverified / false thresholds and a decided_by strip (C, A, P).

Per-threshold chip linked to its source; a false value shows the reserved FALSE ASSUMPTION colour with the old value struck through; a corrected value shows its current_status chip plus a history icon.
Lint report grouped by severity, with a visualization-payload previewer.
modules.method: Define the manifest as JSON Schema 2020-12 with enumerations for category (13), phase (5), jury tags (4), current_status (verified, team_assumption, unverified, false), decided_by (code, ai, person) and runtime tier (T0-T3). Each parameter, threshold and metric carries current_status, history[] and decided_by with actor and date. Validate with Ajv at editor save, registry CI (P15-M05) and graph load (P15-M02). Outputs must match a declarative payload schema drawn by first-party code; Vega specs use the CSP-safe interpreter. A direction-aware manifest-diff tool (v1) suggests a bump. Lint: opened source per verified threshold, relationship text, decided_by present, AI-drafted fields confirmed by a named person before verified, SPDX licence, permissions, fixture per metric, SemVer, unique id, capped extracts. Until P15-M04 ships, only first-party and T0 modules run.

modules.name: Sandbox for community code and visualizations
modules.design_question: How can the platform run community module code, and show its output, without exposing user models, tokens or the host page to malicious or buggy code?
inputs: Module bundle and manifest (runtime tier, permissions, output caps)
Validated input payload (JSON or transferred ArrayBuffer)
Pinned runtime and wheel bytes with SHA-256
Resource limits (time, memory)
outputs: Schema-validated module output and declarative visualization payload
Telemetry {cpu_ms, peak_memory, terminated, denied_calls[]}
Permission-grant record per module@version

parameters.name: runtime_tier (T0 declarative | T1 JS in QuickJS-WASM or SES | T2 Pyodide, dev only | T3 server container)
parameters.relationship: Higher tier -> more expressive, larger attack surface. Pyodide is no security boundary: four of seven products in the Aug 2026 report got no code fix; shipped fixes left in-process Pyodide. Browser T2 is dev-only; T3 is the Python default.

parameters.name: granted_permissions (network, storage, geometry read/write)
parameters.relationship: Default-deny plus declared permissions: each added permission enlarges what a compromised module can read or exfiltrate. Chrome warns users and disables an extension until it accepts a newly added permission.

parameters.name: origin isolation (separate registrable domain; CSP sandbox header)
parameters.relationship: allow-scripts plus allow-same-origin on same-origin content can remove its own sandbox. Serve the sandbox from a separate registrable domain with header 'Content-Security-Policy: sandbox allow-scripts' (opaque origin); a meta tag cannot set it.

parameters.name: csp_placement (on the sandbox document, not the worker)
parameters.relationship: Blob and data workers inherit the creating document's CSP, so the policy sits on the sandbox document's response header (default-src 'none'; script-src with blob: and 'wasm-unsafe-eval'; worker-src blob:; connect-src 'none'). Exact strings are CI-tested per tier.

parameters.name: header_capable_host
parameters.relationship: GitHub Pages cannot set response headers, so the sandbox origin needs a host with a headers file, such as Cloudflare Pages _headers (up to 100 rules); the registry index can stay on Pages.

parameters.name: runtime_bytes_via_host
parameters.relationship: connect-src 'none' also stops a runtime fetching its own .wasm and packages. The host fetches pinned bytes, checks SHA-256 and transfers ArrayBuffers; micropip and network stay off. Feasibility per runtime is untested.

parameters.name: memory, stack and time limits
parameters.relationship: Caps stop runaway modules; QuickJS offers memory, stack and interrupt-deadline limits, whereas SES does not mitigate memory or CPU exhaustion.

parameters.name: cross-origin isolation (COOP and COEP headers, optional)
parameters.relationship: Needed only for SharedArrayBuffer interrupts; default cancel is Worker.terminate. If used, apply COOP/COEP to the run page only, not module pages with cross-origin embeds such as giscus (inference); static hosts need a service-worker shim.

parameters.name: visualization_rendering (declarative payload, host-drawn)
parameters.relationship: Module markup in the host DOM is XSS, and image or CSS URLs can carry Layer 0 data out because img-src, not connect-src, governs them. Modules return declarative payloads (P15-M03); host code renders them; host CSP allowlists img-src and connect-src.

parameters.name: output_caps enforcement
parameters.relationship: Message-boundary checks reject outputs above manifest caps, so a module cannot exhaust host memory or rendering with huge arrays or meshes.

metrics.name: Sandbox-escape suite pass rate
metrics.good: 100% of red-team cases blocked per tier and browser (ctypes, Emscripten exports, fetch, XHR, WebSocket, DOM, storage, parent postMessage, eval, top navigation)
metrics.method: CI red-team suite per tier, seeded with the failure classes from the Aug 2026 Pyodide disclosure.
metrics.basis: Policy threshold; failure classes verified in the Cyera report (seven products affected, including n8n CVE-2025-68668).

metrics.name: Sandbox CSP delivered and denial verified cross-browser
metrics.good: Sandbox document carries the CSP and sandbox header; fetch, WebSocket, importScripts, nested Worker, eval and top navigation are denied in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit, and the blob worker starts
metrics.bad: Any call allowed, or the worker fails to start in any engine
metrics.method: Playwright tests on all three engines against the deployed sandbox origin.
metrics.basis: r1 put a CSP on a worker response inside an opaque-origin iframe on GitHub Pages; MDN says blob and data workers inherit the creator's CSP and Pages cannot send headers. Blob workers in opaque-origin iframes are unconfirmed.

metrics.name: Visualization containment
metrics.good: 0 module-supplied HTML, SVG, URL or style strings reach the host DOM or any network request
metrics.method: Red-team cases for img src, CSS url(), SVG, anchor navigation and oversized payloads; host CSP report-only logging.
metrics.basis: Design policy; img-src governs images, so a connect-src 'none' worker alone does not close this channel.

metrics.name: Permission least-privilege
metrics.good: Used permissions equal declared permissions
metrics.method: Instrument host API calls; compare with manifest.
metrics.basis: Chrome guidance to request only permissions the main function needs.

metrics.name: Runaway-module containment
metrics.good: Module killed within its budget; p98 of scripted discrete interactions <= 200 ms (Event Timing, threshold 16 ms) and p95 frame time <= 33.3 ms during the kill test
metrics.bad: p98 > 500 ms or module not killable
metrics.method: Infinite-loop fixture; watchdog calls Worker.terminate, then removes the iframe; scripted clicks and frame deltas recorded meanwhile.
metrics.basis: Terminate semantics from MDN. INP bands are field p75 and Event Timing hides continuous events and sub-threshold entries; bands are team presets (r1 label verified was wrong).

metrics.name: Resource caps enforced
metrics.good: Memory, time and output caps set and enforced for every tier
metrics.method: Per-tier preset in platform config; numeric defaults set after benchmarking.
metrics.basis: SES explicitly leaves exhaustion unmitigated; QuickJS provides the knobs.

metrics.name: Pyodide cold-start time and download size
metrics.good: unverified: to be benchmarked
metrics.method: Measure first and warm load on a campus network; npm core package unpacked size is 13,879,282 bytes (core only).
metrics.basis: No sourced figure for end-to-end cold start.

metrics.name: Bundle provenance and integrity
metrics.good: 100% of community releases carry a GitHub artifact attestation verified in CI, and the client checks the index SHA-256 before loading
metrics.method: CI runs gh attestation verify; client verifies SHA-256 like subresource integrity.
metrics.basis: npm provenance applies to npm publish, not to file bundles at URLs. GitHub attestations link a bundle to its workflow and commit; they prove origin, not safety.

metrics.name: Python isolation boundary
metrics.good: Published community Python runs only in T3 (server or OS isolation); browser Pyodide is limited to unpublished dev use
metrics.bad: A published module runs in-page Pyodide without process or OS isolation
metrics.method: Registry CI rejects tier T2 for published listings.
metrics.basis: Cyera: four of seven products had no code fix; the fixes that shipped (n8n external runners, Grist Deno, smolagents removing WasmExecutor) left in-process Pyodide.

visualization: Install-time permission card in plain language with icons (reads geometry: yes; network: none; storage: none; CPU and memory caps), modelled on browser extension permission warnings.
Per-node runtime badge: tier T0-T3, shield colour for 'reviewed' vs 'unreviewed community', small live meters for CPU ms and memory.
Red 'terminated' banner with reason; amber 'payload rejected' banner naming the schema rule; sandbox report log with denied calls.
modules.method: Community T1 code runs in a blob Worker inside an iframe served from a separate registrable domain on a header-capable host. The iframe response header sets 'sandbox allow-scripts' plus a CSP (default-src 'none'; script-src 'self' blob: 'wasm-unsafe-eval'; worker-src blob:; connect-src 'none'; img-src 'none'), inherited by the blob worker. The host fetches pinned runtime bytes (SHA-256 checked) and talks to the worker only by postMessage with schema, size and count checks. Output is data plus a declarative visualization payload drawn by host code. A watchdog calls Worker.terminate, then removes the iframe. T1: QuickJS-WASM or SES; T2: browser Pyodide (dev only); T3: gVisor or microVM server job, the default for published Python. CI red-team suite per tier in Chromium, Firefox, WebKit.

Whether a blob worker starts in an opaque-origin iframe in all three engines, and the minimum CSP Pyodide needs, are untested. COEP effects on embeds are inferred. Hardening Pyodide is an arms race.

modules.name: Registry and distribution
modules.design_question: How should modules be published, reviewed, versioned, forked, verified and installed so the community can share them GitHub-style while maintainers keep quality and security?
inputs: Pull request adding a module version (manifest, bundle, tests)
Index repository state
Maintainer review decisions and CI results
Vulnerability reports
outputs: Registry index: one JSON-lines file per module id, one line per version {version, bundle URL, SHA-256, attestation, dependency ranges, tier, permissions, yanked, reason, forked_from}
Installable bundles with GitHub artifact attestations, mirrored by the registry
flags.json kill-switch list read by clients {module@version, threshold id, current_status, history[]}
Fork lineage graph and workspace lockfile entries

parameters.name: index_model (git index repo | sparse static JSON)
parameters.relationship: A git index gives reviewable history and zero server cost; sparse per-file fetching lowers client download. Cargo supports both; Homebrew taps are plain git repositories installed by name.

parameters.name: review_gate (CI plus human approval)
parameters.relationship: Homebrew merges only after CI passes and an organisation member approves; Obsidian review is automated and blocks installation until errors are fixed; Yak describes no review step. Stricter gate -> higher quality, slower publishing.

parameters.name: immutability and yank
parameters.relationship: A published version is never edited; yanking sets a flag so new installs skip it while existing pinned graphs still resolve (Cargo yanked flag; Comfy and Yak versions cannot be overwritten).

parameters.name: version resolution and lockfile
parameters.relationship: Exact pins in the lockfile keep results reproducible; ranges apply to dependencies only, and 0.y.z caret ranges stay inside one minor (^0.2.3 < 0.3.0). ComfyUI stores node versions in workflow JSON for the same reason.

parameters.name: fork lineage (forked_from)
parameters.relationship: A fork is a separate repository linked to upstream, and forks of public repositories are public, so entrants cannot fork the index privately. Track lineage through forked_from plus a CI licence-compatibility check.

parameters.name: naming and namespace
parameters.relationship: Case-insensitive collision checks and treating '-' and '_' as equal reduce confusing or look-alike names (crates.io rules).

parameters.name: bundle_integrity (SHA-256 + attestation + mirror)
parameters.relationship: The index stores a SHA-256 and attestation reference per bundle; the client verifies the hash before loading and CI verifies the attestation. Attestations prove where a bundle was built, not that it is safe; accepted bundles are mirrored.

parameters.name: client_kill_switch (flags.json)
parameters.relationship: Clients fetch flags.json at start and refuse or warn on yanked or blocked versions already in a lockfile, showing the reason; without it a malicious version stays loadable in saved graphs.

parameters.name: hosting limits
parameters.relationship: GitHub Pages allows a 1 GB published site and a 100 GB/month soft bandwidth limit; larger assets such as Python wheels must come from a CDN.

metrics.name: CI gate before merge
metrics.good: 100% of merged module PRs passed all automated checks
metrics.method: Branch protection requires status checks and a CODEOWNERS review.
metrics.basis: Homebrew contributing guide: pull requests with failing CI should not be merged.

metrics.name: Time to first maintainer response
metrics.good: <= 3 days
metrics.method: Median interval from PR open to first non-bot response.
metrics.basis: Editable preset; CHAOSS defines the metric and says to exclude bot replies but gives no numeric bands.

metrics.name: SemVer breaking-change detection
metrics.good: Every schema-breaking change shipped as MAJOR (MINOR inside 0.y.z)
metrics.bad: Breaking change shipped as PATCH, or as MINOR at >= 1.0.0
metrics.method: Automated direction-aware manifest diff in CI (P15-M03).
metrics.basis: SemVer 2.0.0 items 4 and 8.

metrics.name: Published registry size
metrics.good: <= 1 GB
metrics.method: Measure the Pages artifact in CI.
metrics.basis: GitHub Pages published-site limit.

metrics.name: Bundles with verified attestation and matching SHA-256
metrics.method: CI runs gh attestation verify before the index line is accepted; a client integration test checks the hash.
metrics.basis: r1 cited npm provenance, which applies only to npm publish. GitHub artifact attestations (actions/attest) apply to build artifacts such as bundles; the threshold is our policy. Plan eligibility is unverified.

metrics.name: Flagged or yanked versions shown with reason in the client
metrics.method: Client integration test against flags.json and the yanked field.
metrics.basis: Course requirement that wrong claims stay visible.

metrics.name: Time to block a reported malicious version in clients
metrics.good: <= 2 days
metrics.method: Interval from a verified report to a flags.json entry live in clients.
metrics.basis: Editable preset; no sourced benchmark.

visualization: Registry grid with filters by category code, phase, jury tag, licence, tier and status; cards show version, SPDX badge, tests pass/fail, counts of verified and team-assumption thresholds, attestation tick, expert-reviewed badge.
Module detail page: README, manifest summary, source list, version timeline with yanked and FALSE ASSUMPTION markers, dependents.
Fork lineage drawn as a DAG; PR review checklist sidebar with CI status badges.
Install button adds module@version to the workspace lockfile; blocked versions show a red banner with the reason.
modules.method: The registry is a public GitHub repository (index repo) with one JSON-lines file per module id and one line per version, following the Cargo index layout. An author opens a PR adding a version line {version, bundle URL, SHA-256, attestation, dependency ranges, tier, permissions, forked_from}. CI runs manifest lint (P15-M03), fixtures, the sandbox red-team smoke test (P15-M04), the SPDX check, the source-link check and attestation verification. A CODEOWNERS maintainer approves; merge publishes the index through GitHub Pages and mirrors the bundle. Bundles are built by GitHub Actions with actions/attest. Clients verify SHA-256, resolve exact versions into a workspace lockfile and fetch flags.json at start. Yanking flips a flag; other fields never change. Nothing from a user's project is uploaded here (P15-M07).

modules.name: Comments, reviews, ratings and flags
modules.design_question: How do users comment on, review, rate and flag modules or single thresholds so wrong assumptions stay visible, status vocabulary stays single and ratings are not misleading, without exposing entrants' unpublished designs?
inputs: Discussion threads on registry module pages (GitHub Discussions via giscus)
Structured reviews (usefulness vote, evidence link)
Flag submissions {module@version, threshold id, claim, evidence URL, proposed correction, claimed current_status}
outputs: Rating summary {n, positive fraction, Wilson lower bound}
Flag records with current_status, history[], workflow state (open | resolved), affected versions and corrected value
Chip state per threshold; moderation queue

parameters.name: rating_score (Wilson lower bound, z = 1.96)
parameters.relationship: Small samples inflate plain averages; the lower bound ranks 2 of 2 positive ratings at about 0.34 and 180 of 200 at about 0.85 (computed from the formula), so thinly rated modules do not outrank well-tested ones.

parameters.name: min_votes_to_display
parameters.relationship: Below a minimum n the interval is wide, so show 'not enough ratings' instead of a number.

parameters.name: vote_integrity (one vote per GitHub account per major version)
parameters.relationship: Votes parsed from replies are easy to game with several replies or later edits; counting one vote per account per major version and ignoring post-aggregation edits limits inflation. Design logic; n >= 5 is a thin floor.

parameters.name: flag_status_and_state (shared enum + workflow state)
parameters.relationship: A flag carries the shared current_status {verified | team_assumption | unverified | false} plus history[] and a workflow state open or resolved; UNRESOLVED is a state, not a claim status. A flagged claim is never deleted, as OSV keeps introduced, fixed and withdrawn events.

parameters.name: discussion_backend (giscus on GitHub Discussions | own database)
parameters.relationship: giscus stores threads in GitHub Discussions and needs no database, but the repository must be public and users need GitHub accounts, so every thread is public and identity-linked. An own database removes that at the cost of hosting and moderation.

parameters.name: discussion_scope_and_embargo
parameters.relationship: Public, identity-linked threads can expose an entrant's scheme before judging (VTC terms 4.1, 5.1, 5.3). Threads attach to registry module pages only, entrants are told not to discuss their own scheme before results, and none is embedded in project or template views.

parameters.name: moderator_response_time
parameters.relationship: Longer time to first response -> lower perceived activity and weaker contributor retention (CHAOSS objective; no numeric relationship given).

parameters.name: expert vs crowd separation
parameters.relationship: Crowd ratings measure perceived usefulness; expert review (P15-M08) measures correctness. Showing them separately, and never beside the status chip, prevents a popular but wrong module looking verified. Design logic.

metrics.name: Wilson lower-bound rating
metrics.method: Count positive and negative votes; apply the Wilson score formula at 95% confidence.
metrics.basis: Formula and z = 1.96 verified; good/bad cut-offs and minimum n are editable team presets.

metrics.name: Time to first response to comments and flags
metrics.good: <= 3 days
metrics.method: CHAOSS Time to First Response, excluding bot replies.
metrics.basis: Definition verified; bands are presets.

metrics.name: Flag completeness
metrics.good: Every flag with current_status false has evidence URL, corrected value and affected version range
metrics.method: Issue form validation plus maintainer checklist.
metrics.basis: Modelled on the OSV schema fields.

metrics.name: Flag visibility
metrics.good: 100% of flags render with an icon and text label and the reserved colour for false; corrected claims show their current chip plus a history icon
metrics.method: UI test; contrast of the flag colour at least 3:1; comprehension tested in P15-M09.
metrics.basis: Course requirement (flagged claims stay visible); WCAG non-text contrast and use of colour.

metrics.name: Vote integrity
metrics.good: 1 counted vote per GitHub account per module major version; edits after aggregation ignored
metrics.method: Aggregation Action de-duplicates by account and major version; replay test with duplicate and edited replies.
metrics.basis: Design policy against gaming.

metrics.name: Public-thread exposure of unpublished designs
metrics.good: 0 threads or comments on project or template views before the embargo end; module-page threads carry the 'do not discuss your own scheme' notice
metrics.method: UI test of where the giscus embed can load; notice present on every module page.
metrics.basis: r1 text said repository visibility was unverified. giscus states the repository must be public, so all comments are public and tied to GitHub accounts.

visualization: Per-threshold chip following current_status: green verified, amber team assumption, grey unverified, reserved magenta-red false with the old value struck through and the corrected value beside it; a history icon marks corrected claims; hover shows source and flag history.
Rating histogram with a Wilson-interval whisker and an 'n' label, placed apart from the status chips.
Version strip showing affected and fixed version range, in OSV style.
Embedded giscus thread under each registry module page with a visible privacy notice; moderation queue for maintainers.
modules.method: Each registry module page embeds a giscus thread mapped to the module id; threads are for module feedback, and entrants are told not to discuss their own scheme before results. Structured reviews are replies using a template (vote plus evidence link); a GitHub Action parses them into ratings.json, counting one vote per account per major version and ignoring later edits. Ratings use the Wilson lower bound (z = 1.96), hidden below the minimum n. Flags come from an Issue form recording {module@version, threshold id, claim, evidence URL, proposed value, claimed current_status}. Maintainers set status and state; an Action writes flags.json and never deletes entries. The client overlays flags on chips using the shared enum; a corrected claim keeps the old value struck through and links to the corrected version. Expert badges are separate (P15-M08). Ships after 30 Nov.

GitHub API rate limits were not verified. COEP require-corp on a page embedding the cross-origin giscus iframe would likely block it (inference). modules.name: Local-first projects, VTC-safe sharing and workflow templates
modules.design_question: How do projects stay private and recoverable on one device, exports pass an anonymity scan before upload, templates get shared safely after the embargo, and modules switch on or off without silently breaking downstream results?
inputs: Graph JSON (P15-M01) and RunRecords (P15-M02)
Layer 0 payload (kept local)
Registry index and lockfile (P15-M05, v1)
Flags and yanked versions (P15-M06, v1)
User on/off choices and the embargo end date
outputs: Local project store with revision history and last-backup time
Graph-JSON hand-off file with a basic diff (added and removed nodes and edges, changed parameters)

parameters.name: storage_model (local-first OPFS/IndexedDB, no server copy by default)
parameters.relationship: Design data stay in the browser, so unpublished visuals are not reachable by others. OPFS is origin-bound and is deleted when site data are cleared; it is not synced across devices as far as MDN states.

parameters.name: persistence_and_backup (persist() plus export reminders)
parameters.relationship: Call navigator.storage.persist() at first save and show the result: best-effort data can be evicted under storage pressure, and Safari may delete script-written data after 7 days without interaction. Persistence does not stop the user clearing data, so remind to export daily and on close.

parameters.name: publish_gate (static notice in core, dialog in v1)
parameters.relationship: VTC terms 4.1 require visuals not previously published and 5.1/5.3 require no identifying marks, so publish, fork, share, template upload and comment embeds warn first until the embargo end. The gate is a warning, not legal advice; 'published' is undefined.

parameters.name: embargo_end_date (explicit, editable)
parameters.relationship: Terms 5.3: the jury learns identities only after winners are selected; 10.7 lets evaluation be extended and no results date is stated. The gate stays on until the entrant sets a date (default unset), so risk after 30 Nov is covered.

parameters.name: template_export_scope (graph, parameters and pins by default; geometry, renders, outputs opt-in)
parameters.relationship: Geometry and renders reveal the scheme while module pins and parameters mostly do not, so only the latter export by default; the rest need explicit opt-in and an embargo date. Previews are drawn from graph JSON, not screenshots. Design logic.

parameters.name: collaboration_model (core: single writer + file hand-off | roadmap: CRDT)
parameters.relationship: A 2-4 person team shares one graph by passing a graph-JSON file with a basic diff, so only one person edits at a time. A CRDT such as Yjs merges concurrent edits, but y-webrtc needs signalling servers and any relay sees unencrypted data.

parameters.name: revision_history (undo/redo, revision id per RunRecord)
parameters.relationship: Each graph revision gets an id and each RunRecord stores it, so users can see which graph produced which numbers; undo creates a new revision and never edits a past record. Design logic.

parameters.name: lockfile pins (module@exact version)
parameters.relationship: Pinning keeps results reproducible when a module later changes; ComfyUI stores node versions in workflow JSON so workflows can be reproduced.

parameters.name: toggle semantics (the single enum of P15-M02)
parameters.relationship: Block is the default; bypass only through a declared passthrough pair, with downstream results stamped. Delete is an edit, not a toggle. Mixed semantics would change what a downstream pass/fail means. Design logic.

parameters.name: template licence
parameters.relationship: Graph JSON and docs are content (CC BY 4.0 suits); code keeps an OSI licence. Creative Commons advises against CC licences for software.

parameters.name: embedded third-party material
parameters.relationship: Never embed the brief, site model or Buildner presentation template package: 7.5.5 forbids redistributing the templates, 7.5.6 keeps the organiser's IP, and no licence for the brief is stated. Link and cite instead.

parameters.name: export_anonymity (required pre-upload scan)
parameters.relationship: Terms 4.7 bar changes after first upload without a fee, so the scan runs before upload and stamps 'scan passed' with file hashes. Metadata scans catch EXIF/XMP and PDF fields; OCR (v1) catches visible names; panels are JPEG up to 10 MB (4.8).

metrics.basis: Policy derived from VTC terms 4.1, 5.1 and 5.3 (risk of identification or prior publication); not legal advice.

modules.name: Governance, licensing and expert-reviewed badge
modules.design_question: What contribution rules, licences, expert-review process and Indigenous-content notices keep the open-source tool trustworthy, lawful, and honest about what it does not evaluate?
inputs: Repository health files
Contributor submissions and AI-use disclosures
Reviewer pool and review threads
Licence declarations from manifests and dependency trees
Vulnerability reports
outputs: Core: LICENSE, README and the CULT palette notice
After 13 Nov: CONTRIBUTING, CODE_OF_CONDUCT, SECURITY; v1: GOVERNANCE, content-licence matrix, CODEOWNERS
Community-health checklist and Scorecard result
Review records {module@version, reviewers, expertise, thread URL, date} driving the badge
Licence audit report and the Indigenous-content hold list

parameters.name: governance_model (BDFL | meritocracy | liberal contribution)
parameters.relationship: A small student-run project can start with named maintainers and a written contributor process, formalising later; documenting how someone becomes a maintainer in GOVERNANCE.md reduces the 'private clique' perception.

parameters.name: code_of_conduct text, version and reporting route
parameters.relationship: Contributor Covenant 3.0 is CC BY-SA 4.0, so derived texts must share alike; it needs a real contact and an enforcement ladder. Use a role mailbox plus a backup recipient (e.g. course staff), not one student's address.

parameters.name: code vs content licence
parameters.relationship: Code under an OSI-approved licence (MIT or Apache-2.0); documentation and templates under CC BY 4.0. Creative Commons recommends against CC licences for software and allows them for documentation and artistic elements.

parameters.name: review depth for the expert-reviewed badge
parameters.relationship: rOpenSci uses two external reviewers in a public thread; JOSS checks OSI licence, tests and documentation. More reviewers -> more confidence but longer lead time; the optimal number has no evidence.

parameters.name: CODEOWNERS and branch protection
parameters.relationship: Requiring a code-owner review makes an owner of each path approve changes to it; owners need write access or their approval is not requested.

parameters.name: AI-use disclosure (as decided_by)
parameters.relationship: Homebrew requires disclosure of AI/LLM use and personal accountability; JOSS has an AI policy for reviews. Here disclosure is a manifest field: decided_by = ai on AI-drafted values until a named person confirms them (P15-M03).

parameters.name: indigenous_data_hold_rule
parameters.relationship: CARE (collective benefit, authority to control, responsibility, ethics) puts Indigenous Peoples in charge of data about them. Hard rule: nothing representing Musqueam, Squamish or Tsleil-Waututh cultural knowledge is listed without documented Nation-authorised involvement; students never self-certify consent.

parameters.name: cult_palette_notice (user-facing statement)
parameters.relationship: The CULT palette and first-run screen say: no Nation-authorised modules exist for VTC 2026 and this tool does not evaluate cultural context. That criterion carries 30% of the jury score, so an empty palette must not read as a pass.

parameters.name: cultural_context_30 tag disclaimer
parameters.relationship: The tag says a module evidences that criterion, not that any Nation endorses it. Reviewers assign it, it is never self-assigned, and its card carries a no-endorsement notice. Design logic, unsourced.

parameters.name: advisory_route (UBC SALA, First Nations House of Learning)
parameters.relationship: OCAP and Nation protocols stay unread (403 on 21 Oct). DRIPA binds provincial law, not a student project. A named owner (team to fill) contacts UBC SALA and the First Nations House of Learning by 4 Nov 2026 (team target); until confirmed, content stays held.

parameters.name: brief and third-party redistribution
parameters.relationship: VTC 7.5.5 forbids redistributing the Presentation Template Package and 7.5.6 keeps organiser IP; no licence for the brief or site model is stated. Treat all as all-rights-reserved (team assumption); store citations and derived parameters only.

parameters.name: standards_text_policy
parameters.relationship: NBC/VBBL, ASHRAE and CSA documents are copyrighted: modules cite clause numbers and store derived thresholds; reviewers reject copied tables or clauses; manifest extracts are length-capped (P15-M03). Team policy, not legal advice.

parameters.name: vulnerability_disclosure_and_takedown
parameters.relationship: SECURITY.md names a private reporting channel; a confirmed malicious version is yanked and pushed to clients through flags.json (P15-M05). Response targets are editable presets.

metrics.name: GitHub community-profile completeness
metrics.good: README, code of conduct, CONTRIBUTING, LICENSE, security policy and issue templates all present
metrics.method: Read the repository's community profile.
metrics.basis: GitHub community profile checklist.

metrics.name: OpenSSF Scorecard aggregate
metrics.method: Run Scorecard on the registry and tool repositories in CI.

metrics.name: Expert-reviewed badge criteria
metrics.good: >= 2 independent reviewers with declared expertise, public review thread, passing tests, OSI licence
metrics.bad: Badge shown without a thread or with fewer than 2 reviewers
metrics.method: Badge is issued only when a review record exists and links to the thread.
metrics.basis: Practice taken from rOpenSci (two reviewers, badge links to thread) and JOSS (OSI licence, tests); adopting it here is our decision.

metrics.name: Licence audit
metrics.good: 100% of modules have a valid SPDX licence and compatible licences for npm dependencies and runtime-loaded WASM wheels or Pyodide packages
metrics.bad: Any module without a licence, or an unaudited runtime package
metrics.method: Parse manifests, dependency trees and runtime package lists.
metrics.basis: SPDX list; a missing licence leaves no reuse right.

metrics.name: Brief and Buildner template files in the registry
metrics.method: Hash and filename scan against the VTC downloads and the Buildner template package.
metrics.basis: r1 basis said only that no redistribution licence is stated; terms 7.5.5 and 7.5.6 also bar redistribution of the template package.

metrics.name: Indigenous-content listing check
metrics.good: 100% of listings that represent Musqueam, Squamish or Tsleil-Waututh knowledge, or carry a cultural_context_30 tag, have a recorded Nation-authorised involvement and a no-endorsement notice
metrics.method: Reviewer checklist item plus a CI check for the record.
metrics.basis: Our policy, informed by CARE (authority to control); not sourced to any Nation's protocol, which could not be read.

metrics.name: CULT palette notice shown
metrics.good: 100% of CULT palette views and the first-run screen show the no-Nation-authorised-modules notice
metrics.method: UI test of palette and first-run screens.
metrics.basis: Policy: users must not infer cultural-context support from an empty palette.

metrics.name: Advisory-route contact made
metrics.good: Owner named in the decision log and first contact with UBC SALA and the First Nations House of Learning made by 4 Nov 2026
metrics.bad: No owner or no contact by that date
metrics.method: Check the decision log; record replies or silence.
metrics.basis: Team target; neither office's response time is known. Owner name was not in the materials given to this revision.

metrics.name: Conduct reporting route
metrics.good: Role mailbox plus a named backup recipient who is not a student maintainer
metrics.method: Read CODE_OF_CONDUCT (after 13 Nov).
metrics.basis: Policy; Contributor Covenant needs a real contact and the guide advises a backup admin.

visualization: Governance dashboard: health checklist with ticks linked to files on GitHub, Scorecard gauge 0-10.
CULT palette banner: 'No Nation-authorised modules for VTC 2026. This tool does not evaluate cultural context.'
Badge on each module card: 'Expert-reviewed' (tooltip lists reviewers, expertise, date, thread), 'First-party', 'Held for Indigenous review', or none.

modules.method: Core by 13 Nov: LICENSE (code), README, the CULT palette notice and the hold rule. After 13 Nov: LICENSE-content (CC BY 4.0), CONTRIBUTING (module PR checklist: manifest, sources opened, decided_by, tests, licence, AI-use disclosure, no copied standards text), CODE_OF_CONDUCT (Contributor Covenant 3.0 with CC BY-SA notice, role mailbox, backup recipient), SECURITY, then GOVERNANCE and CODEOWNERS per category. Expert review: maintainers invite two reviewers; review happens in a public thread against a checklist; on approval a review record is added and the badge links to the thread. CI runs Scorecard and the licence audit. Content representing Musqueam, Squamish or Tsleil-Waututh knowledge is held until Nation-authorised involvement is documented; cultural_context_30 tags carry a no-endorsement disclaimer.

modules.name: Formative usability evaluation, onboarding and starter template
modules.design_question: Can target designers wire Layer 0 to a check, read a RunRecord, tell who decided each value and find a FALSE ASSUMPTION unaided, and which design changes follow before entrants rely on the tool?
inputs: Thin pilot build (Layer 0 import, starter graph, run-all, RunRecord table, outline view) by 8 Nov 2026
Three task scripts, chip and provenance quiz, consent text
5-8 participants from outside the build team
Cognitive-dimensions checklist
outputs: Findings table with severity and decision (fix, defer, accept)
Per-task success, time, wiring errors, time to first result
Chip, provenance and stale-result comprehension scores
VTC starter graph template and first-run guide

parameters.name: participant_count (5-8, think-aloud, rounds of about five)
parameters.relationship: About five users find roughly 85% of problems in a first round, and several small rounds beat one large; Davis et al. used four students. Fewer users miss problems; more add little per round.

parameters.name: task_set (wire to a check; read a RunRecord; find a FALSE ASSUMPTION)
parameters.relationship: The tasks fix what is measured: wiring tests port rules, RunRecord reading tests provenance, the FALSE ASSUMPTION task tests the chip vocabulary. Changing tasks between rounds breaks comparison.

parameters.name: measures (success, time, wiring errors, comprehension)
parameters.relationship: Unaided success, time on task, wiring errors and quiz accuracy show where the tool misleads. Think-aloud gives reasons but no strong statistics, and prompts can bias behaviour.

parameters.name: cognitive_dimensions_walkthrough (viscosity, hidden dependencies, secondary notation)
parameters.relationship: Viscosity is effort to change, hidden dependencies are links not visible, secondary notation is labels and layout outside syntax. Davis et al. found unnamed, unclustered Grasshopper scripts hard to read, so these are the likely weak points.

parameters.name: schedule (pilot by 10 Nov; follow-up after 30 Nov)
parameters.relationship: Entrants get 17 days (13-30 Nov) with the tool, so pilot findings must land before core is frozen on 13 Nov. A second round after 30 Nov checks the fixes and informs the 10 Dec final.

parameters.name: ethics_route (QI use versus research)
parameters.relationship: Sessions used only to improve the tool may fall outside REB review under TCPS 2 Article 2.5; publishing results as research would need review. UBC's own rule is unchecked, so ask the course team first.

parameters.name: starter_template (Layer 0 -> FSR, height band, daylight)
parameters.relationship: A pre-modularised, labelled starter graph gives entrants a readable first graph and tests the whole path in the pilot. Check modules come from other packets; only first-party T0 modules that exist by 6 Nov are included.

parameters.name: pilot_status_notice
parameters.relationship: State on first run that VTC 2026 is a pilot: entrants are not the first users and the tool is untested at scale. Honest labelling lets entrants weigh results and keep their own checks.

metrics.name: Unaided task success
metrics.good: >= 80% of task attempts completed without help
metrics.method: Facilitator marks success; help given counts as failure.
metrics.basis: Team presets; no sourced band for node editors.

metrics.name: Time to first result
metrics.good: <= 15 min from first run to a RunRecord on the starter graph
metrics.method: Stopwatch from first screen to first RunRecord.
metrics.basis: Team presets for a 17-day entrant window.

metrics.name: Wiring errors per task
metrics.good: <= 1, each recovered using the rejection tooltip
metrics.method: Count rejected connections and wrong-but-accepted wires in the session log.
metrics.basis: Team presets; tests typed-port design.

metrics.name: Status chip comprehension
metrics.good: >= 90% correct readings of verified, team assumption, unverified, false and the corrected-history icon
metrics.method: Quiz of 8 chips shown without legend.
metrics.basis: Team presets; tests the single enum and history icon.

metrics.name: Provenance comprehension (decided_by)
metrics.good: >= 80% of participants state who decided a given threshold
metrics.method: Ask participants to read the strip on a node card.
metrics.basis: Team presets; course rule on separating code, AI and people.

metrics.name: Stale-result recognition
metrics.good: >= 90% of stale results identified as stale
metrics.method: Edit an input and ask which numbers are current.
metrics.basis: Team presets; tests the auto and run-all defaults.

metrics.name: Graph explainability
metrics.good: >= 4 of 5 reviewers explain the starter graph's main flow within 5 minutes
metrics.method: Timed explanation by teammates who did not build the graph.
metrics.basis: Team presets; Davis et al. link clear names and structure to legibility.

metrics.name: Cognitive-dimensions walkthrough completed
metrics.good: Viscosity, hidden dependencies and secondary notation each assessed with a fix or an accepted decision
metrics.method: Two team members walk the three tasks and log findings.
metrics.basis: Green and Petre framework; adoption here is our decision.

metrics.name: Pilot timing
metrics.good: Sessions held by 10 Nov and a follow-up round after 30 Nov
metrics.bad: No session before entrants rely on the tool
metrics.method: Check the session log dates.
metrics.basis: Team schedule against the 13 Nov core and 30 Nov deadline.

visualization: Findings table sorted by severity with owner and decision.
Per-task dot plot of time and success per participant.
Confusion matrix of status-chip quiz answers.
First-run guide: 5-minute tour, 'what each chip and strip means' card, pilot banner.
modules.method: Build a thin pilot (Layer 0 import, starter graph, run-all, RunRecord table, outline view) by 8 Nov. Recruit 5-8 M.Arch or VTC-style designers outside the build team. Each does three think-aloud tasks (wire massing to an FSR or daylight check; read a RunRecord and say who decided each threshold; find the FALSE ASSUMPTION), then a chip and provenance quiz and a 5-minute graph-explanation task. Record success, time, wiring errors, time to first result and quiz accuracy; screen-record with consent. Two team members run a cognitive-dimensions walkthrough. Fix, retest informally, and repeat with a fresh group after 30 Nov. Findings go into the change log with severity and decision; bands are team presets.

libraries.role: Scripted session logging and regression of fixed findings

modules.effort: About 0.3 dev-week for scripts, 5-8 sessions, walkthrough and fixes triage; follow-up round after 30 Nov about 0.2 week (team estimate). Core total with this is about 3.3 against about 3 of capacity (see notes).
modules.human_judgment: Which findings are fixed, deferred or accepted, whether a failure is a design or participant problem, and when a facilitator prompts stay with the team.
modules.limits: 5-8 designers cannot support statistics; bands are team presets; participants are students, not VTC jurors or practising architects; the pilot build is thinner than core; Davis et al. studied four students on Grasshopper only. UBC ethics rule unchecked.
jury_criteria: No direct jury criterion; checks that evidence chips and provenance are readable for all four tags.
