sources.title: Pyodide - Keyboard interrupts
sources.extract: Interrupt with a SharedArrayBuffer passed to setInterruptBuffer; must run in a worker; server must send the headers SharedArrayBuffer requires.

sources.title: Sandcastles, Not Sandboxes: How One Architectural Flaw Exposed Seven Products
sources.extract: Published 7 Aug 2026: Python-level denylists in Pyodide sandboxes missed ctypes and Emscripten exports. Status table: n8n (CVE-2025-68668, CVSS 9.9) fixed by external runners; Grist fixed by moving to Deno; smolagents removed its opt-in WasmExecutor; cohere-terrarium ctypes path unpatched and repository archived; langchain-sandbox archived, no fix described; stlite and cibuildwheel made no code changes (deployer responsibility). Mitigations: allowlist, strip exports, OS-level isolation, least privilege; Python controls are not the sole boundary.

sources.title: MDN - Using Web Workers
sources.extract: Workers are in general not governed by the CSP of the creating document; an eval example shows a worker can use eval when the page cannot. Exception: if the worker script's origin is a globally unique identifier (data or blob URL) it inherits the creator's CSP. A worker's own CSP comes from a header on its script response. The page does not mention sandboxed iframes.

sources.title: MDN - iframe element (sandbox attribute)
sources.extract: Without allow-same-origin content gets a unique opaque origin; allow-scripts plus allow-same-origin on same-origin content lets it remove the sandbox; serve untrusted content from a separate origin.

sources.title: MDN - Window.crossOriginIsolated
sources.extract: Cross-origin isolation requires COOP same-origin and COEP require-corp or credentialless; needed to use SharedArrayBuffer.

sources.title: MDN - Worker.terminate()
sources.extract: Immediately stops a Web Worker without letting it finish pending operations.

sources.title: WebAssembly - Security
sources.extract: Modules run in fault-isolated sandboxes with bounds-checked linear memory and control-flow integrity; side channels, race conditions and overflows within linear memory remain possible.

sources.title: SES (Secure ECMAScript) - Endo
sources.extract: lockdown() freezes intrinsics; Compartments start with no ambient authority; limits: guests can run forever and allocate unlimited memory; availability and exhaustion threats not mitigated. Repository licence shown as Apache-2.0.

sources.title: quickjs-emscripten
sources.extract: QuickJS compiled to WebAssembly; memory limits, stack limits and interrupt/deadline handlers; host functions exposed explicitly; MIT per npm.

sources.title: Deno - Security and permissions
sources.extract: Default-deny permissions; --allow-run and --allow-ffi are equivalent to allow-all; for untrusted code use layered defence: minimal permissions, Web Worker, OS sandboxing, and gVisor or Firecracker VMs.

sources.title: coi-serviceworker
sources.extract: MIT; enables COOP/COEP via service worker on hosts such as GitHub Pages that cannot set headers; must be a separate same-origin file; first load triggers a reload.

sources.title: Chrome extensions - Permission warnings
sources.extract: Permissions declared in the manifest; some trigger install-time warnings; optional permissions requested at runtime; an update adding a warned permission disables the extension until accepted.

sources.title: VS Code - Extension manifest
sources.extract: package.json fields: lowercase unique name, SemVer version, publisher, engines.vscode (not *), fixed categories list, activationEvents, contributes, license.

sources.title: JSON Schema specification
sources.extract: Current version is 2020-12 (previous 2019-09); Core and Validation specifications plus meta-schemas.

sources.title: Ajv JSON Schema validator
sources.extract: MIT; supports drafts 2020-12, 2019-09, 07 (04 via separate package); fast validator for Node.js and browsers.

sources.title: Semantic Versioning 2.0.0
sources.extract: Declare a public API; MAJOR for incompatible changes (item 8), MINOR for compatible features, PATCH for fixes; major version zero (0.y.z) is for initial development where anything may change (item 4); released versions must not be modified.

sources.title: Cargo - Registry index format
sources.extract: Git or sparse index; one file per package with one JSON line per version (vers, deps, cksum, yanked); entries immutable except yanked; crates.io naming rules (case-insensitive collisions, '-' and '_' equivalent).

sources.title: Homebrew - How to create and maintain a tap
sources.extract: A tap is a git repository of formulae (name homebrew-*); install via brew install user/repo/formula; non-official taps need trust; semantic version tags recommended.

sources.title: homebrew-core CONTRIBUTING
sources.extract: PR tested locally then CI; failing CI should not be merged; an organisation member must approve; BrewTestBot merges; AI/LLM use must be disclosed and the contributor answers for it.

sources.title: Obsidian - Submit your plugin
sources.extract: README, LICENSE, manifest.json required; version x.y.z must match the release tag; id unique across plugins; review is automatic and errors block installation.

sources.title: Yak - The package manifest
sources.extract: manifest.yml with required name, version, authors, description and recommended url, keywords, icon; SemVer 2.0.0 or four-digit System.Version; restricted name characters.

sources.title: Yak - Pushing a package to the server
sources.extract: yak login with a Rhino Account; first pusher owns the package; versions cannot be deleted or overwritten, only yanked; no review or moderation step mentioned; test server wiped nightly.

sources.title: Comfy Registry - Overview
sources.extract: Registry for custom nodes: semantic versioning, published versions immutable, deprecation, globally unique names, workflow JSON stores node versions, nodes scanned for malicious behaviour and given a verification flag.

sources.title: npm - Generating provenance statements
sources.extract: Needs npm 9.5.0+, a supported cloud CI (GitHub Actions or GitLab CI) and --provenance on npm publish (or trusted publishing); signed via Sigstore and logged publicly; applies to packages on the npm registry, with a public repository field; does not guarantee the package is free of malicious code. The page does not cover non-npm files.

sources.title: OSV schema
sources.extract: JSON format for vulnerabilities: id, modified, published, withdrawn, aliases, affected packages with SEMVER/ECOSYSTEM/GIT ranges and introduced/fixed events, references. Used here as the model for status history events.

sources.title: GitHub Pages limits
sources.extract: Published site max 1 GB; source repo recommended 1 GB; 100 GB/month soft bandwidth; 10 builds/hour soft (not for custom Actions workflows).

sources.title: GitHub Docs - About forks
sources.extract: A fork is a separate repository linked to upstream; fork network shares git data; upstream owners can read all forks; public repository forks are public, and a fork's visibility cannot be changed by itself.

sources.title: giscus repository
sources.extract: MIT; comments and reactions stored in GitHub Discussions, no database; users authorise via GitHub OAuth; moderation on GitHub; self-hosting possible.

sources.title: How Not To Sort By Average Rating
sources.extract: Wilson score lower bound = [p + z^2/2n - z*sqrt((p(1-p) + z^2/4n)/n)] / (1 + z^2/n); z = 1.96 for 95% confidence.

sources.title: CHAOSS metric - Time to First Response
sources.extract: Interval between creation of an item needing attention and first response; exclude bot responses; no numeric good/bad bands given.

sources.title: web.dev - Interaction to Next Paint (INP)
sources.extract: Good <= 200 ms; needs improvement up to 500 ms; poor > 500 ms, evaluated at the 75th percentile of page loads recorded in the field. Per visit INP is the longest interaction ignoring outliers (the web-vitals library takes the 98th percentile). Lab INP depends on which interactions are performed; Total Blocking Time is a possible proxy but not a substitute.

sources.title: Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.2
sources.extract: SC 1.4.3 contrast 4.5:1 (3:1 large text); SC 1.4.11 non-text contrast 3:1; SC 2.1.1 keyboard operability (only the first 100,000 characters of the page were read).

sources.title: Understanding SC 2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum)
sources.extract: Pointer targets at least 24 by 24 CSS pixels unless spacing (24 px circles must not intersect other targets), equivalent, inline, user-agent or essential exception applies (Level AA); independent of page zoom; overlapping area is excluded from target size; dense visualisations and maps are essential-exception examples. CSS transforms are not discussed.

sources.title: Understanding SC 2.5.7 Dragging Movements
sources.extract: Any drag action needs a simple single-pointer alternative (Level AA). Examples: map plus direction buttons; click one item then another to draw a connecting line; selection mode with two corner clicks; slider track click. Keyboard equivalence does not automatically meet it. Node editors are not mentioned.

sources.title: Contributor Covenant 3.0 Code of Conduct
sources.extract: Stewarded by the Organization for Ethical Source and licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0; four-rung enforcement ladder (warning, temporarily limited activities, temporary suspension, permanent ban).

sources.title: GitHub Docs - About community profiles for public repositories
sources.extract: Checklist of README, code of conduct, contributing guide, licence, security policy and issue templates.

sources.title: GitHub Docs - About code owners
sources.extract: CODEOWNERS in .github/, root or docs/; last matching pattern wins; owners need write access; branch protection can require code-owner review.

sources.title: OpenSSF Scorecard
sources.extract: Apache-2.0; checks score 0-10 with risk weights (Critical 10, High 7.5, Medium 5, Low 2.5); examples Code-Review, Branch-Protection, Signed-Releases, Dangerous-Workflow.

sources.title: JOSS review criteria
sources.extract: OSI-approved licence file, statement of need, installation and usage docs, community guidelines, automated tests or documented manual tests, sustained development history, AI usage disclosure.

sources.title: rOpenSci software peer review - introduction
sources.extract: Two external reviewers per submission, associate editor, public review thread as a GitHub issue; accepted packages show a peer-reviewed badge linking to the review.

sources.title: Open Source Guides - Leadership and governance
sources.extract: Governance models (BDFL, meritocracy, liberal contribution); document how to become a maintainer in GOVERNANCE.md; use an organisation with a backup admin.

sources.title: Creative Commons FAQ
sources.extract: Recommends against CC licences for software (CC0 is the exception); CC licences may be used for documentation and separate artistic elements (only first 100,000 characters of the page were read).

sources.title: SPDX License List
sources.extract: Short identifiers for licences, with an OSI-approved column; expressions combine identifiers with WITH and +.

sources.title: Vancouver Tall Challenge - Terms and conditions
sources.extract: Visual materials must not have been previously published (4.1); panels are JPEG up to 10 MB (4.8); no identifying marks (5.1); jury learns identities only after winners are selected (5.3); 4.7 bars modifying or re-uploading a submission after first upload without a fee; 7.5.5 forbids redistributing the Presentation Template Package and 7.5.6 keeps organiser IP; 10.7 lets evaluation be extended, no results date stated; 11.1 prize announced on the portal; no clause on AI or software tools.

sources.title: GIDA - CARE Principles for Indigenous Data Governance
sources.extract: Page text read supports Collective Benefit and Authority to Control only; Responsibility and Ethics were not defined in the portion retrieved (see the Carroll et al. paper, P15-S72, for all four).

sources.title: Food4Rhino
sources.extract: Named in the scope as a distribution precedent; the site returned HTTP 403, so publishing, rating and moderation practices were not verified.

sources.title: giscus - configuration and requirements
sources.extract: The repository must be public (otherwise visitors cannot view the discussion), the giscus app must be installed, and Discussions must be enabled.

sources.title: MDN - Content-Security-Policy: sandbox directive
sources.extract: The sandbox directive applies an iframe-like sandbox to the resource it is sent with; without allow-same-origin the origin is opaque ('null'); it is not supported in a meta element, so it must be an HTTP header.

sources.title: MDN - Content-Security-Policy: script-src
sources.extract: Without 'wasm-unsafe-eval' (or 'unsafe-eval') in script-src, WebAssembly is blocked when a CSP is present; 'wasm-unsafe-eval' allows WebAssembly without allowing eval() or Function(). The page does not describe worker-src fallbacks.

sources.title: MDN - Content Security Policy (CSP) guide
sources.extract: img-src sets allowed sources for images; default-src is the fallback for fetch directives not listed and 'none' blocks a resource type entirely. The page does not describe connect-src or form-action in detail.

sources.title: RFC 8785 - JSON Canonicalization Scheme (JCS)
sources.extract: Informational RFC; serialises JSON numbers as IEEE 754 doubles using ECMAScript number-to-string rules; sorts object properties recursively by UTF-16 code units; array order unchanged; NaN and Infinity are errors.

sources.title: ECMAScript language specification - Math object function properties
sources.extract: The intro to the Math function properties says the behaviour of functions such as sin and exp is not precisely specified and some latitude is allowed in the choice of approximation algorithms; Math.sin and Math.exp return implementation-approximated values.

sources.title: GitHub Docs - Using artifact attestations to establish provenance for builds
sources.extract: Add the actions/attest step with subject-path to attest a binary or file; verify with 'gh attestation verify PATH -R ORG/REPO'; workflow permissions id-token: write, contents: read, attestations: write. Plan eligibility is not stated on the page.

sources.title: GitHub Docs - Artifact attestations (concepts)
sources.extract: Attestations are signed claims linking an artifact to its workflow, repository, commit and triggering event; public repositories use the Sigstore Public Good Instance, private ones GitHub's Sigstore instance; they do not prove the artifact is secure, and consumers set their own policy.

sources.title: The CARE Principles for Indigenous Data Governance (Carroll et al., Data Science Journal)
sources.extract: Four principles: Collective Benefit (data should advance Indigenous communities' development and outcomes), Authority to Control (Indigenous Peoples determine data governance protocols), Responsibility (respectful, lasting relationships), Ethics (Indigenous Peoples assess benefits, harms and future uses).

sources.title: Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples Act (SBC 2019, c 44)
sources.extract: Affirms the application of the UN Declaration to BC's laws; section 3 requires measures to make provincial laws consistent with the Declaration, section 4 an action plan prepared with Indigenous peoples.

sources.title: Vega - Expression interpreter
sources.extract: By default Vega builds functions with the Function constructor, which violates CSP script-src without unsafe-eval; the vega-interpreter evaluates the expression AST instead and is CSP-compliant, about 10% slower on average.

sources.title: MDN - Origin private file system
sources.extract: OPFS is private to the page's origin and not visible to the user; clearing site storage deletes it; subject to browser quota; the page does not state whether it syncs across devices.

sources.title: React Flow - Accessibility
sources.extract: Nodes and edges are keyboard-focusable by default (Tab); Enter or Space selects; Escape clears; selected nodes move with arrow keys (Shift for speed; disableKeyboardA11y turns this off); an aria-live region announces movements. No keyboard connection is documented. The page says React Flow 'can help' meet WCAG 2.1 AA when properly implemented.

sources.title: React Flow - ReactFlow component API reference
sources.extract: connectOnClick true; isValidConnection validates a new connection; nodesDraggable true, panOnDrag true, selectionOnDrag false (selectionKeyCode Shift), edgesReconnectable true (reconnectRadius 10), panOnScroll false; nodesFocusable and edgesFocusable true; minZoom 0.5, maxZoom 2; onlyRenderVisibleElements false and adds some overhead.

sources.title: Cloudflare Pages - Headers
sources.extract: A _headers file in the output directory sets custom response headers; up to 100 header rules, 2,000 characters per line; not applied to Pages Functions responses. Pricing is not stated on the page.

sources.title: node-semver (npm semver) README
sources.extract: Caret ranges allow changes that do not modify the left-most non-zero element: ^0.2.3 means >=0.2.3 <0.3.0-0 and ^0.0.3 means >=0.0.3 <0.0.4-0; ISC licence.

sources.title: Buildner - Resubmit your design
sources.extract: A concept may be reused, but if the presentation materials were already published they must be visually updated before submission and be visually distinct from earlier versions; unpublished materials may be submitted as they are; the page says nothing about anonymity.

sources.title: Yjs repository
sources.extract: MIT; CRDT framework with shared types merged without conflicts; network agnostic with offline support; y-indexeddb persists documents in the browser; y-webrtc is peer-to-peer but exchanges signalling data over signalling servers.

sources.title: Vancouver Tall Challenge - competition page and brief download
sources.extract: The brief PDF and site model sit behind an email form with no direct URL, so the brief itself was not opened. r1 cited this page for the true-north angle; it supports no angle value, so r2 removed that citation. The FAQ says a previously published concept may be resubmitted by its author.

sources.title: Contributor Covenant 2.1 Code of Conduct
sources.extract: The page states no licence for the text; it says only that it is adapted from the Contributor Covenant. Version 3.0 states CC BY-SA 4.0.

sources.title: mathjs - Expression security
sources.extract: The expression parser is sandboxed and avoids eval and new Function (since v4) but the docs warn of unknown vulnerabilities; functions such as import, evaluate and parse can be disabled; heavy expressions can exhaust memory, so run them in a worker that can be killed.

sources.title: FNIGC - OCAP principles
sources.extract: Named as the First Nations data-governance standard (ownership, control, access, possession); the page returned HTTP 403 in r1 and again on 21 Oct 2026 (r2), so its text was not read; no archived copy was used.

sources.title: Response Times: The 3 Important Limits
sources.extract: 0.1 s feels instantaneous; 1 s keeps flow of thought; 10 s keeps attention. Over 1 s show the system is working; over 10 s give a percent-done indicator and a clearly signposted way to interrupt.

sources.title: Event Timing API (W3C Working Draft)
sources.extract: Working Draft of 13 Oct 2026. mousemove, pointermove, pointerrawupdate, touchmove, wheel and drag are continuous events that are not exposed. Default durationThreshold 104 ms, minimum 16 ms; durations rounded to 8 ms.

sources.title: MDN - PerformanceEventTiming
sources.extract: Entries below durationThreshold (default 104 ms, minimum 16 ms) are not reported; durations are rounded to the nearest 8 ms; exposed types cover click, keyboard, pointer down/up, touch start/end and drag-and-drop events; Baseline 2025 (newly available).

sources.title: MDN - Long animation frame timing
sources.extract: Reports animation frames over a fixed 50 ms threshold with script and render timings; use PerformanceObserver (buffer holds 200 entries). The compatibility table was not shown, so support outside Chromium is unverified.

sources.title: McNeel wiki - Data stream matching algorithms
sources.extract: Shortest List stops when the shortest stream runs out; Longest List is the default and keeps connecting until all streams run dry, shorter streams staying at their last value in the example; Cross Reference makes every combination (100 points in the example).

sources.title: React Flow - MiniMap component
sources.extract: pannable (default false) pans the viewport by dragging in the minimap; zoomable (default false) zooms by scrolling; default aria label 'Mini Map'; onNodeClick handles clicks on minimap nodes.

sources.title: React Flow - Edge type
sources.extract: Per-edge reconnectable (boolean or HandleType) overrides edgesReconnectable and lets an edge be updated by dragging its source or target; ariaRole defaults to 'group'.

sources.title: React Flow - ReactFlowInstance type
sources.extract: Methods include setViewport, getViewport, zoomIn (factor 1.2), zoomOut, setCenter, fitView and updateNode; panBy is not listed, so button panning uses setViewport.

sources.title: React Flow - Controls component
sources.extract: Zoom in/out, fit view and interactive-lock buttons, shown by default; container aria-label 'React Flow controls'; per-button labels and keyboard focusability are not stated.

sources.title: Understanding visual scripts: Improving collaboration through modular programming (Davis, Burry, Burry)
sources.extract: Survey of 1,982 Grasshopper scripts by 575 designers: 56% had no named parameters, 97.5% no clusters. Think-aloud tests with four students: modular scripts were far easier to understand; inputs left, outputs right, colour separation and clear names helped; inline explanations were seldom read.

sources.title: Usability analysis of visual programming environments: a cognitive dimensions framework (Green and Petre)
sources.publisher: Journal of Visual Languages and Computing 7, 131-174
sources.extract: Not opened: the DOI redirected to a publisher page with no text. Citation and scope taken from the opened Green and Blackwell tutorial (P15-S97), which adapts it.

sources.title: Cognitive Dimensions of Information Artefacts: a tutorial v1.2 (Green and Blackwell)
sources.extract: Hidden dependency: a dependency that is not fully visible. Viscosity: resistance to change. Secondary notation: extra information outside formal syntax (layout, labels). Also premature commitment, visibility and abstraction.

sources.title: Why You Only Need to Test with 5 Users
sources.extract: About five users find roughly 85% of problems in a first test (model N(1-(1-L)^n), L about 31%); several small rounds beat one large study; 3-4 users per group for distinct user groups.

sources.title: Thinking Aloud: The #1 Usability Tool
sources.extract: Users verbalise while doing tasks; reveals misconceptions at low cost with a few users; caveats: no detailed statistics, unnatural speech, facilitator prompts can bias behaviour.

sources.title: MDN - StorageManager.persist()
sources.extract: Resolves true if storage is made persistent (cleared only by explicit user action), else false; the browser decides; secure contexts only; not available in Workers; Baseline widely available since 2021.

sources.title: MDN - Storage quotas and eviction criteria
sources.extract: Best-effort data can be evicted LRU by origin under storage pressure; persistent data only by user action; Firefox prompts, Safari and Chromium decide silently; Safari may delete script-created data after 7 days without interaction when tracking prevention is on; eviction is all-or-nothing per origin.

sources.title: City of Vancouver Open Data - Public streets (API records)
sources.extract: Street segments as GeoJSON LineStrings with hblock names. Our computation from six downtown block segments: Granville St about 44.6 deg and W Georgia St about 134-135 deg from true north (geodesic bearings, derived, not published). Licence text not read.

sources.title: Vancouver's deviant grids (Villagomez)
sources.extract: Describes a 45 degree grid of the city centre against the city's north-south grid; qualitative, not a surveyed angle against true north.

sources.title: UBC SALA home page
sources.publisher: UBC School of Architecture and Landscape Architecture
sources.extract: Land acknowledgement to the Musqueam people and a commitment to reconciliation; no Indigenous advisory body, role or contact found on the home or strategic-directions pages; the contact page was not opened. UBC Indigenous portal and First Nations House of Learning URLs redirected to a status page on 21 Oct 2026.

sources.title: PROV-O: The PROV Ontology
sources.extract: W3C Recommendation, 30 Apr 2013. Core classes Entity, Activity, Agent (Person, SoftwareAgent, Organization); properties wasAttributedTo, wasGeneratedBy, wasAssociatedWith, actedOnBehalfOf. First 100,000 of about 262,900 characters read.

sources.title: Understanding SC 1.4.1 Use of Color
sources.extract: Colour must not be the only visual means of conveying information or distinguishing an element (Level A); text cues, patterns and icons are named techniques.

sources.title: TCPS 2 (2022) Chapter 2, Article 2.5
sources.extract: Quality assurance and improvement studies, program evaluation and testing within normal educational requirements are not research under the Policy when used only for assessment, management or improvement; later research use is secondary use and may need REB review. UBC's own rule not read.

sources.title: P14 packet r3: Layer 0 schema (P14-M01) and units, true north, georeferencing (P14-M03)
sources.extract: P14-M01 defines the Layer 0 JSON Schema with semver schema_version, 13 typed classes and staged documents Draft, Georef, Checked, Complete. P14-M03 defines true_north_deg, north_type and a derived street-grid bearing of 44.7 and 134.7 deg from 969 parcels. Internal, derived figures.

flags.claim: Pyodide/WebAssembly isolation is enough to run untrusted community Python safely in the browser.
flags.correction: Treat Pyodide as one layer only. A 7 Aug 2026 disclosure showed escapes in seven products (ctypes and Emscripten exports reached the JS host). Add host-level isolation (separate origin, CSP on the sandbox document, no network), allowlists, stripped exports, maintainer review, or run server-side in a sandbox.
flags.detail: WebAssembly's own docs list side channels and in-memory overflows as remaining risks; two of the seven products received no fix because maintainers treated isolation as the deployer's job (corrected in r1: four of seven got no code fix, see below).

flags.claim: A Web Worker created by our page inherits the page's Content-Security-Policy and is therefore a safe place for community code.
flags.correction: Workers are generally not governed by the creating document's CSP; a worker script must be served with its own CSP header (blob: and data: workers inherit). Workers also still have network access unless blocked.
flags.detail: MDN: a page with script-src 'self' blocks eval(), yet code in a worker it creates can still call eval().

flags.claim: litegraph.js (or its Comfy fork) is a maintained, safe choice for the node canvas.
flags.correction: Original litegraph.js last pushed 2024-08-01 with about 1.2 k weekly downloads; the Comfy-Org fork is archived (2026-01-14). Use @xyflow/react (pushed 2026-10-20, about 8.3 M weekly downloads) with Rete as the fallback.
flags.detail: Observed 21 Oct 2026 from GitHub API and npm download API.

flags.claim: A keyboard alternative satisfies the drag requirement ('Single-pointer or keyboard alternative to drag', WCAG 2.5.7).
flags.correction: Provide single-pointer, non-drag alternatives (click source then target, select then nudge or click destination, numeric size fields) and test keyboard operability separately under SC 2.1.1.
flags.detail: The Understanding page states that keyboard equivalence does not automatically meet SC 2.5.7 and that the two are evaluated independently (opened 21 Oct 2026, P15-S50). Affected metric: P15-M01 'Single-pointer non-drag alternative for every drag action'. Scope widened in r2 (see r2 flag on drag inventory).

flags.claim: A sandboxed community worker can carry its own CSP response header (connect-src none) inside an opaque-origin iframe, with the sandbox hosted on GitHub Pages.
flags.correction: Put the CSP and the sandbox directive on the sandbox iframe document's response header, on a header-capable separate domain; the blob worker inherits it. Test denial of fetch, WebSocket, importScripts, nested Worker, eval and top navigation in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit.
flags.detail: MDN: blob and data workers inherit the creating document's CSP; only a worker with a normal URL uses its own response header (P15-S18). The coi-serviceworker page notes GitHub Pages cannot set headers (P15-S27). That an opaque-origin document can only start blob or data workers is an inference from same-origin worker fetch rules and stays unverified.

flags.claim: INP thresholds are 'verified' for measuring canvas interaction latency in a test build at the 75th percentile.
flags.correction: Reclassified as team_assumption. Use a scripted interaction set and report Event Timing p98 per session, with Total Blocking Time as a secondary lab proxy.
flags.detail: web.dev defines the bands at the 75th percentile of field page loads; lab INP depends on which interactions are scripted; web-vitals uses the 98th percentile (P15-S47). Affected metrics: P15-M01, P15-M02, P15-M04. r2: the measurement method was corrected again (see r2 flag on Event Timing and continuous events).

flags.claim: The VTC terms say nothing that restricts redistribution of competition materials, and only anonymity constrains entrants' publishing.
flags.correction: Never host Buildner's Presentation Template Package in modules or templates. Treat sharing design visuals before judging as a risk under 4.1, and keep projects local by default.
flags.detail: Terms 7.5.5 forbid redistribution, resale or sharing of the template package; 7.5.6 keeps the organiser's IP; 4.1 says visual materials must not have been previously published; the resubmission page requires previously published visuals to be visually updated (P15-S60, P15-S80). The terms have no clause on posting entries to social media, and 'published' is undefined.

flags.claim: Whether giscus needs a public repository is unknown.
flags.correction: giscus requires a public repository with the giscus app installed and Discussions enabled, so all comments are public and tied to GitHub accounts; module-page threads only, with a privacy notice.
flags.detail: giscus.app states the repository must be public, otherwise visitors cannot view the discussion (P15-S64). The earlier UNVERIFIED flag is resolved by this.

flags.claim: npm provenance provides signed provenance for registry module bundles.
flags.correction: Use GitHub artifact attestations (actions/attest) on bundle files, verify them in CI with gh attestation verify, and have the client check the index SHA-256; mirror accepted bundles.
flags.detail: npm provenance is generated by npm publish --provenance for packages on the npm registry; bundles at URLs in a JSON-lines index are not npm packages (P15-S40). GitHub attestations link a file to its workflow and commit and prove origin, not safety (P15-S70, P15-S71).

flags.claim: Two of the seven products in the Aug 2026 Pyodide disclosure received no fix.
flags.correction: Four of seven (cohere-terrarium, langchain-sandbox, stlite, cibuildwheel) had no code fix; the three fixes that shipped (n8n external runners, Grist Deno, smolagents removing WasmExecutor) moved or removed in-process Pyodide. Make T3 the Python default and keep browser Pyodide as a dev tier.
flags.detail: Cyera status table read 21 Oct 2026 (P15-S17): cohere-terrarium ctypes path unpatched and archived; langchain-sandbox archived with no fix described; stlite and cibuildwheel made no code changes.

flags.claim: Scripting a drag and recording Event Timing durations measures canvas drag latency (M01, M02 and M04 latency metrics).
flags.correction: Use Event Timing (durationThreshold 16 ms) only for discrete interactions, p98 over all scripted interactions with unreported ones counted as 16 ms. Measure drag, pan and zoom as frame times (requestAnimationFrame deltas; Long Animation Frames secondary).
flags.detail: W3C Event Timing lists mousemove, pointermove, pointerrawupdate, touchmove, wheel and drag as continuous events that are not exposed; MDN gives the 104 ms default, 16 ms minimum and 8 ms rounding (P15-S87, P15-S88). A p98 over reported entries only is biased toward slow events.

flags.claim: Incremental re-run bands (good <= 5 s, bad > 30 s) have no sourced benchmark (M02).
flags.correction: Rebase on Nielsen's limits: good <= 1 s for T0 and formula nodes, acceptable <= 10 s, bad > 10 s unless a percent-done indicator and a Cancel control are shown. Marked as a sourced HCI guideline applied by our reading.
flags.detail: Nielsen (1993, updated 2014): 0.1 s instantaneous, 1 s flow of thought, 10 s attention; over 10 s a percent-done indicator and a signposted interrupt (P15-S86). A 30 s band loses designer attention in the parameter-tweak loop.

flags.claim: Connect, move and resize are the drag actions needing single-pointer alternatives (M01 SC 2.5.7 metric).
flags.correction: Inventory all drag props: pan (panOnDrag), edge reconnect (edgesReconnectable), marquee (selectionOnDrag, Shift-drag) and minimap pan too; give each a click alternative or disable it, and test by enumerating enabled props.
flags.detail: React Flow defaults panOnDrag true and edgesReconnectable true (P15-S77); MiniMap pannable is a drag (P15-S91); SC 2.5.7 examples give map direction buttons and click-click alternatives (P15-S50).

flags.claim: Longest-list matching is design logic supported by P15-S12.
flags.correction: Cite McNeel's data-stream-matching page (P15-S90): Longest List is Grasshopper's default and shorter streams keep their last value. Keep it for familiarity, stamp repeated items in the RunRecord and on the wire, and offer strict matching for metric nodes.
flags.detail: P15-S12 covers data trees only and gives no matching rules. Silent repetition can create a pass/fail result nobody asked for.

flags.claim: MIT licensing of React Flow means the on-canvas attribution can be removed without paying.
flags.detail: The vendor states attribution may be removed only with a Pro subscription (Starter $169/month, Professional $289/month) while the library itself stays MIT. Whether MIT legally obliges the on-canvas badge was not verified; default is to leave it visible. Board and template images are drawn by our own SVG exporter, so no canvas badge is baked in; whether exports need the badge is also unverified.

unresolved_relationships: Graph size (node and edge count) vs canvas frame time and recompute time in React Flow: the performance guide gives no figures; needs a benchmark.
Frame-time bands (p95 <= 16.7 ms good, > 33.3 ms bad) vs perceived smoothness on mid-range laptops: 16.7 ms is the 60 Hz budget only; no sourced band for node-editor drag.
Pyodide package set and cold-start time vs user abandonment: no sourced numbers; measure first and warm loads.
Number of expert reviewers vs defect escape rate for community modules: rOpenSci uses two but gives no evidence of the optimum.
Rating count and Wilson score vs actual module correctness: the statistic handles sampling uncertainty only; no source links crowd ratings to correctness.
Review response time vs contributor retention in a student-run registry: CHAOSS names the objective but gives no numeric relationship.
Sandbox permission granularity vs contributor and user friction: no sourced evidence.
Execution-mode default (auto for T0 and formula nodes, run-all for heavy nodes) vs stale-number misreading and user trust: no sourced evidence; tested in the P15-M09 pilot.
Auto debounce length (preset 250 ms) vs wasted re-runs and perceived instantness: Nielsen gives the 0.1 s and 1 s limits but no debounce value.
Longest-list repetition vs rate of silent pass/fail errors in metric nodes: McNeel documents the behaviour, no error-rate data.
Template granularity (nodes per template) vs reuse and learning: no sourced evidence.
Disabled-node mode (bypass vs block) vs correctness of downstream verdicts: design logic only, not empirically sourced.
Effect of COEP require-corp or credentialless on third-party embeds (giscus, map tiles) and on Pyodide interrupts: not verified.
Canvas zoom level vs rendered handle size (React Flow minZoom default 0.5) and the zoom threshold below which handles hide: inferred, needs measurement against WCAG 2.5.8.
Number of category hue families (13 codes, cap 8 plus lightness) vs distinguishability under colour-vision deficiency: no sourced limit; text codes carry the meaning.
Designer comprehension of status chips, the corrected-history icon and the decided_by strip vs misuse of evidence: untested until the P15-M09 pilot.
Wiring-error rate and time to first result for M.Arch designers on the starter graph: no data until the pilot.
Minimum CSP that QuickJS-WASM and Pyodide need to start (wasm-unsafe-eval alone vs unsafe-eval): not found in the sources read; settle in the CI denial suite.
Whether an opaque-origin sandboxed iframe can start a blob Worker in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit: inferred, not verified.
Cross-engine numeric differences in module outputs vs the tolerance needed per metric type: ECMAScript allows approximation but no sourced magnitudes.
Output size and list-length caps vs memory exhaustion or rendering freeze: no sourced figures; benchmark.
Graph size vs RunRecord size and export time: no sourced figures.
Whether sharing work-in-progress visuals (private link, public repository, social post) counts as 'previously published' under VTC 4.1: terms undefined; ask Buildner.
Time from vulnerability report to client-side block vs exposure of users with the module in their lockfiles: no sourced benchmark.
Local-first storage eviction and clearing vs risk of losing a design: MDN gives eviction rules (LRU, Safari 7-day) but no rates; persist() grant rate per browser is unknown.
CRDT collaboration relay (signalling or sync server) vs exposure of unpublished designs: Yjs notes signalling servers; no analysis of confidentiality options.

Street-grid bearing (about 44.7 deg) and the VTC block's own frame vs shadow direction error: derived from parcels and street segments, not from the site plan arrow; fixture to compare shadow azimuth at solar noon (true north) before sun modules ship.
Overlap of P14-M06 and P15-M07 (versioning, provenance, anonymised export): which packet owns the store and the scan is undecided.
Core scope of about 3.3 dev-weeks (including the pilot) vs about 3 dev-weeks of capacity before 13 Nov: absorbed only by the cut order in the notes; capacity itself is an assumption.

case_studies.tool: Grasshopper ecosystem: Yak package manager and Food4Rhino
case_studies.what_it_does: Yak packages Grasshopper plug-ins with a manifest.yml (name, version, authors, description), installs them through Rhino's Package Manager, and lets owners push versions that cannot be overwritten, only yanked. Food4Rhino is the named community download site.
case_studies.workflow_step: Distribution and discovery of analysis plug-ins
case_studies.how_used: Designers find a plug-in, install it, wire it into a definition by hand.
case_studies.strengths: Simple manifest, SemVer or four-digit versions, immutable versions with yank, ownership by first pusher.
case_studies.stops_at: The Yak push page describes no review or moderation step and no sandbox; it records no per-threshold sources or assumptions. Food4Rhino could not be opened.
case_studies.ai_opportunity: Automated manifest lint, source-link checking and test running before listing.
case_studies.ai_wont_improve: Judging whether a plug-in's thresholds are right for Vancouver policy.

case_studies.ai_opportunity: Pattern-based scanning and triage of new versions.

case_studies.tool: rOpenSci software peer review and JOSS
case_studies.what_it_does: Public, expert peer review of software: rOpenSci uses two external reviewers and gives a badge linking to the review thread; JOSS checks OSI licence, tests, documentation and development history.
case_studies.how_used: Authors submit; reviewers work through a checklist in a public GitHub thread.
case_studies.strengths: Transparent, named reviewers, badge points to evidence.
case_studies.stops_at: Neither source defines reviewer qualifications in a way we can copy; both review software quality, not architectural correctness.
case_studies.ai_opportunity: Pre-filling the checklist (licence, tests, links) for reviewers.
case_studies.ai_wont_improve: Expert judgment on wind, structure or planning thresholds.

case_studies.tool: Node-canvas libraries: React Flow (xyflow) vs Rete vs Baklava vs litegraph
case_studies.what_it_does: React Flow renders custom nodes, handles and validation hooks; Rete adds a pull-based dataflow engine with caching; Baklava is Vue-based with an engine and interface types; litegraph.js is canvas-based with typed slots.
case_studies.how_used: Embedded as the editor and, for Rete and Baklava, the engine.
case_studies.strengths: All MIT. xyflow has by far the largest use (about 8.3 M weekly downloads), active pushes, click-to-connect on by default and documented keyboard focus and arrow-key moves; Rete has a built-in cached dataflow engine.
case_studies.stops_at: React Flow has no execution engine or domain port typing, documents no keyboard connect, and enables panOnDrag and edgesReconnectable by default (drag-only); its validation hook guards UI wiring only; litegraph.js is stale and its Comfy fork archived; Baklava has small adoption.
case_studies.ai_wont_improve: Deciding what the port-type vocabulary should be.
case_studies.license_cost: MIT for all four; React Flow Pro is optional and starts at $169/month for attribution removal.

case_studies.tool: Grasshopper visual scripts in practice (Davis, Burry and Burry study)
case_studies.what_it_does: Survey of 1,982 shared Grasshopper scripts plus think-aloud tests with four architecture students comparing modular and unstructured scripts.
case_studies.workflow_step: Reading and modifying someone else's visual graph
case_studies.how_used: Designers share scripts on a forum; peers must understand them to modify them.
case_studies.strengths: Shows what helps legibility: modules, clear names, inputs left and outputs right, colour separation; supplies a think-aloud method for architects.
case_studies.stops_at: Four students and Grasshopper only; no test of status chips, provenance or evidence tools; inline explanations were seldom read.
case_studies.ai_opportunity: Suggesting group labels and parameter names from node behaviour.
case_studies.ai_wont_improve: Whether a graph expresses the designer's intent.
